decisions.choice: the word of the LORD that came to Joel: the heading of the whole book
decisions.reason: The same heading opens Hosea, Micah and Zephaniah. It presents everything that follows, the lament over the locusts, the call to return, the promises and the judgment of the nations, as one message from the LORD given through one man.

decisions.choice: Joel son of Pethuel: the prophet, known only from this book; the book gives no date
alternatives: a date in the ninth century BC, in the reign of King Joash
a date after the exile, in the Persian period
decisions.reason: Nothing is known of Joel or his father Pethuel beyond this verse. The name Joel means "the LORD is God" and was common (1 Samuel 8:2; 1 Chronicles 5:4). Unlike Hosea, Amos or Micah, the heading names no king, and the book never mentions one. It speaks of the temple, its priests and the elders (1:9, 13-14), of Tyre, Sidon and Philistia selling people of Judah to the Greeks (4:4-6), and of Egypt and Edom (4:19). From these hints the book has been dated anywhere from the ninth century BC to after the return from exile, in the fifth or fourth century BC. Its message does not depend on the date.

decisions.choice: The word of the LORD which came to (L); The LORD's word came to (B); This is the message the LORD gave to (R)
decisions.reason: The heading follows the wording set for the Twelve, as in Hosea 1:1. Readable says "message" for "word" and turns the heading into a sentence.

decisions.choice: "Palabra del SEÑOR que vino a" (L); "Este mensaje del SEÑOR vino a" (B); "Este es el mensaje que el SEÑOR le dio a" (R); "Joel hijo de Petuel"
alternatives: La palabra del SEÑOR que vino a Joel
decisions.reason: The heading of the Twelve as Spanish Hosea 1:1 and Micah 1:1 word it at each level. The prophet is "Joel", as Acts 2:16 in Spanish, and his father "Petuel". Book-wide choice for Joel.

decisions.choice: {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, with the article and any preposition inside the span ("del SEÑOR" / "de Yahvé")
decisions.reason: The divine name is a reader setting, as in the published Spanish prophets: the default "el SEÑOR" in small capitals, the alternative "Yahvé". Spanish needs the article only with the title, so the article and its contraction go inside the span. Book-wide choice for Joel.

decisions.choice: "La parole du SEIGNEUR qui fut adressée à" (L); "La parole du SEIGNEUR fut adressée à" (B); "Voici le message que le SEIGNEUR a donné à" (R); "Joël fils de Petouël"
decisions.reason: The heading of the Twelve as the French Hosea 1:1 and Micah 1:1 word it at each level, with the passé simple of a written heading at L and B. The prophet is "Joël" (Acts 2:16) and his father "Petouël". Book-wide choice for Joel.

decisions.choice: {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, with "du SEIGNEUR" / "de Yahvé", "au SEIGNEUR" / "à Yahvé"; the vocative "SEIGNEUR" with no article
decisions.reason: The divine name is a reader setting, as in the published French prophets; the article and its contraction belong to the title only, so they go inside the span. Book-wide choice for Joel.

decisions.choice: "Neno la BWANA lililomjia" (L); "Neno la BWANA lilimjia" (B); "Huu ndio ujumbe ambao BWANA alimpa" (R); "Yoeli mwana wa Pethueli"
decisions.reason: The heading of the Twelve as Swahili Hosea 1:1 words it at each level. The prophet is "Yoeli", as Acts 2:16, and his father "Pethueli". Book-wide choice for Joel.

decisions.choice: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}
decisions.reason: The divine name is a reader setting, as in the published Swahili prophets: "BWANA" in capitals by default, "Yahwe" as the alternative. Swahili has no article, so the span holds the name alone. Book-wide choice for Joel.

decisions.choice: "Lời của CHÚA đã đến với" (L); "Lời CHÚA đến với" (B); "Đây là sứ điệp CHÚA ban cho" (R); "Giô-ên con trai Phê-thu-ên"
decisions.reason: The heading of the Twelve as Vietnamese Hosea 1:1 and Micah 1:1 word it at each level. The prophet's name is the published "Giô-ên" (Acts 2:16); his father is "Phê-thu-ên". Book-wide choice for Joel.

decisions.choice: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, with particles outside the span
decisions.reason: The divine name is a reader setting, as in the published Vietnamese prophets: "CHÚA" in capitals by default, "Gia-vê" as the alternative. Book-wide choice for Joel.

decisions.choice: "…에게 임한 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 말씀" (L); "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 말씀이 …에게 임했다" (B); "이것은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 …에게 주신 말씀이다" (R); "브두엘의 아들 요엘"
decisions.reason: The heading of the Twelve as Korean Hosea 1:1 words it at each level. The prophet is "요엘" (Acts 2:16) and his father "브두엘", in the term sheet's spelling. Book-wide choice for Joel.

decisions.choice: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}, with every particle outside the span
decisions.reason: The divine name is a reader setting, as in the published Korean prophets: "주" by default, "야훼" as the alternative. Both end in a vowel, so particles (의, 께서, 를) stay outside; Korean has no deity_pronoun spans. Book-wide choice for Joel.

decisions.choice: A palavra do SENHOR que veio a (L); A palavra do SENHOR veio a (B); Esta é a mensagem que o SENHOR deu a (R); Joel, filho de Petuel
alternatives: Palavra do SENHOR, que foi dirigida a
decisions.reason: The heading uses the formula of the prophets' headings in Jeremiah ("A palavra ... que veio a Jeremias"), so the books of the Twelve open alike. The names take their plain Portuguese forms, "Joel" and "Petuel".

pt.R: Ouçam isto, anciãos! \q Escutem, todos os que moram na terra! \q Alguma vez aconteceu uma coisa assim durante a vida de vocês, \q ou durante a vida dos seus antepassados?

decisions.choice: the elders: the old people of the community, who were also its leaders
decisions.reason: The word means old people and, from them, the leaders of a town or people. Here the prophet appeals to those whose memory goes back furthest: no one alive has seen anything like this. In 1:14 and 2:16 the same word is used of those gathered for the fast.

decisions.choice: the inhabitants of the land: the people of Judah
decisions.reason: The "land" here is the land of Judah, the LORD's land (1:6; 2:18), not the whole earth. The people addressed are those who live there and gather at the temple in Jerusalem (1:14).

decisions.choice: has this happened in your days or your fathers' days?: nothing like it has ever been seen
decisions.reason: The question expects the answer no. It recalls the locust plague of Egypt, which neither the fathers nor the fathers' fathers of the Egyptians had seen (Exodus 10:6, 14). Joel's disaster is described as being as great as that one.

decisions.choice: your ancestors (B, R); your fathers (L)
decisions.reason: "Fathers" here means the generations before, so Balanced and Readable say "ancestors". Readable says "in your lifetime" for "in your days".

decisions.choice: plural_you on every command and "you" to the elders and the people
decisions.reason: The prophet speaks to the elders and all who live in the land as a group, so every plural "you", verbs and possessives included, takes a plural_you span, as in Joel 2-4.

decisions.choice: present, future and passé composé at every level in chapter 1
decisions.reason: The lament of chapter 1 is the prophet's speech, not narrative, so French uses the tenses of speech at every level, as for Joel 2-4 (recorded at 2:1); "vous" to the elders and the people, who are many.

decisions.choice: Ouçam ... escutem (plural imperatives, "vocês")
decisions.reason: The prophet calls a whole group, so the imperatives are the plural of "vocês" (docs/portuguese-style.md, section 4); the archaic "vós" forms are not used. This holds for the book's calls to the elders, priests, farmers and people.

source.text: עָלֶ֖יהָ לִבְנֵיכֶ֣ם סַפֵּ֑רוּ וּבְנֵיכֶם֙ לִבְנֵיהֶ֔ם וּבְנֵיהֶ֖ם לְד֥וֹר אַחֵֽר׃

vi.L: Hãy thuật lại điều ấy cho con cái các ngươi, \q và [để] con cái các ngươi [thuật lại] cho con cái của họ, \q và con cái của họ cho một thế hệ khác.
vi.B: Hãy kể lại điều ấy cho con cái các ngươi, \q để con cái các ngươi kể lại cho con cái mình, \q và con cái họ kể lại cho thế hệ sau.
vi.R: Hãy kể chuyện này cho con cái các ngươi. \q Hãy để chúng kể lại cho con cái mình, \q và để những đứa con ấy kể lại cho những người đến sau.

ko.L: 이 일을 너희 자녀들에게 이야기하고, \q 너희 자녀들은 그들의 자녀들에게 [이야기하고], \q 그들의 자녀들은 다른 세대에게 [이야기하게 하여라].
ko.B: 이 일을 너희 자녀들에게 들려주어라. \q 너희 자녀들은 자기 자녀들에게 들려주고, \q 그 자녀들은 그다음 세대에게 들려주게 하여라.
ko.R: 이 일을 너희 자녀들에게 이야기해 주어라. \q 그들도 자기 자녀들에게 이야기해 주고, \q 그 자녀들도 뒤에 올 사람들에게 이야기해 주게 하여라.

pt.L: Contem sobre isso aos seus filhos, \q e [que] os seus filhos [contem] aos filhos deles, \q e os filhos deles, a outra geração.
pt.B: Contem isso aos seus filhos, \q e que os seus filhos contem aos filhos deles, \q e os filhos deles, à geração seguinte.
pt.R: Contem isso aos seus filhos. \q Que eles contem aos filhos deles, \q e que esses filhos contem às pessoas que vierem depois.

decisions.choice: tell: the one verb serves for the whole chain of generations
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses the verb once and lets it carry through the next two lines: each generation is to pass the story on to the next.

decisions.choice: telling children and grandchildren: as the LORD's deeds in Egypt were to be told
decisions.reason: In Exodus 10:2, just before the locust plague, the LORD tells Moses to recount his deeds to his son and grandson. Psalm 78:4-6 speaks of telling the next generation the LORD's works. Here what must be remembered is a disaster, and what the LORD will do after it.

decisions.choice: children at every level
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word is the usual word for sons, used for children of both sexes; "children" says that at every level. Literal supplies "let" and "tell" in brackets, which the Hebrew leaves to be carried over from the first line.

decisions.choice: os seus filhos, os filhos deles, with no gender setting
decisions.reason: Portuguese "filhos" already includes daughters (docs/pentateuch-portuguese-terms.md), so there is no second wording to offer and the English choice of "children" needs no span.

source.text: יֶ֤תֶר הַגָּזָם֙ אָכַ֣ל הָֽאַרְבֶּ֔ה וְיֶ֥תֶר הָאַרְבֶּ֖ה אָכַ֣ל הַיָּ֑לֶק וְיֶ֣תֶר הַיֶּ֔לֶק אָכַ֖ל הֶחָסִֽיל׃

records.literal_gloss: [What] remained of the cutting locust, has eaten the swarming locust; and [what] remained of the swarming locust, has eaten the hopping locust; and [what] remained of the hopping locust, has eaten the stripping locust.

en.L: What the cutting locust left, the swarming locust has eaten; \q and what the swarming locust left, the hopping locust has eaten; \q and what the hopping locust left, the stripping locust has eaten.
en.B: What the cutting locust left, the swarming locust has eaten. \q What the swarming locust left, the hopping locust has eaten, \q and what the hopping locust left, the stripping locust has eaten.
en.R: One swarm of locusts after another has come. \q What one swarm left, the next swarm ate, \q and what that swarm left, still another ate.

es.L: Lo que dejó la langosta cortadora, lo ha comido la langosta migratoria; \q y lo que dejó la langosta migratoria, lo ha comido la langosta saltadora; \q y lo que dejó la langosta saltadora, lo ha comido la langosta devoradora.
es.B: Lo que dejó la langosta cortadora, lo devoró la langosta migratoria. \q Lo que dejó la langosta migratoria, lo devoró la langosta saltadora, \q y lo que dejó la langosta saltadora, lo devoró la langosta devoradora.

fr.L: Ce qu’a laissé la sauterelle qui ronge, la sauterelle en essaim l’a dévoré ; \q et ce qu’a laissé la sauterelle en essaim, la sauterelle qui bondit l’a dévoré ; \q et ce qu’a laissé la sauterelle qui bondit, la sauterelle qui dévaste l’a dévoré.
fr.B: Ce que la sauterelle qui ronge a laissé, la sauterelle en essaim l’a mangé. \q Ce que la sauterelle en essaim a laissé, la sauterelle qui bondit l’a mangé, \q et ce que la sauterelle qui bondit a laissé, la sauterelle qui dévaste l’a mangé.
fr.R: Des nuées de sauterelles sont venues, l’une après l’autre. \q Ce qu’une nuée avait laissé, la suivante l’a mangé, \q et ce que celle-là avait laissé, une autre encore l’a mangé.

sw.L: Kilichosazwa na nzige wakataji, nzige wa makundi wamekila; \q na kilichosazwa na nzige wa makundi, nzige warukaji wamekila; \q na kilichosazwa na nzige warukaji, nzige waharibifu wamekila.
sw.B: Kile ambacho nzige wakataji waliacha, nzige wa makundi wamekila. \q Kile ambacho nzige wa makundi waliacha, nzige warukaji wamekila, \q na kile ambacho nzige warukaji waliacha, nzige waharibifu wamekila.
sw.R: Kundi moja la nzige baada ya jingine limekuja. \q Kile ambacho kundi moja liliacha, kundi lililofuata lilikila, \q na kile ambacho kundi hilo liliacha, kundi jingine tena lilikila.

vi.L: Những gì châu chấu cắn phá để lại, châu chấu đàn đã ăn; \q và những gì châu chấu đàn để lại, châu chấu non đã ăn; \q và những gì châu chấu non để lại, cào cào ăn trụi đã ăn.
vi.B: Những gì châu chấu cắn phá chừa lại, châu chấu đàn đã ăn mất. \q Những gì châu chấu đàn chừa lại, châu chấu non đã ăn mất, \q và những gì châu chấu non chừa lại, cào cào ăn trụi đã ăn mất.
vi.R: Hết đàn châu chấu này đến đàn châu chấu khác đã kéo đến. \q Những gì đàn này để lại, đàn sau ăn hết, \q và những gì đàn ấy để lại, một đàn khác lại ăn hết.

ko.L: 자르는 메뚜기가 남긴 것을 떼 지어 다니는 메뚜기가 먹었고, \q 떼 지어 다니는 메뚜기가 남긴 것을 뛰는 메뚜기가 먹었으며, \q 뛰는 메뚜기가 남긴 것을 갉아 먹는 메뚜기가 먹었다.
ko.B: 자르는 메뚜기가 남긴 것은 떼 지어 다니는 메뚜기가 먹어 치웠다. \q 떼 지어 다니는 메뚜기가 남긴 것은 뛰는 메뚜기가 먹어 치웠고, \q 뛰는 메뚜기가 남긴 것은 갉아 먹는 메뚜기가 먹어 치웠다.
ko.R: 메뚜기 떼가 잇달아 몰려왔다. \q 한 떼가 남긴 것을 다음 떼가 먹었고, \q 그 떼가 남긴 것을 또 다른 떼가 먹었다.

pt.L: O que o gafanhoto cortador deixou, o gafanhoto migrador comeu; \q e o que o gafanhoto migrador deixou, o gafanhoto saltador comeu; \q e o que o gafanhoto saltador deixou, o gafanhoto devorador comeu.
pt.B: O que o gafanhoto cortador deixou, o gafanhoto migrador comeu. \q O que o gafanhoto migrador deixou, o gafanhoto saltador comeu, \q e o que o gafanhoto saltador deixou, o gafanhoto devorador comeu.
pt.R: Veio um enxame de gafanhotos depois do outro. \q O que um enxame deixou, o enxame seguinte comeu, \q e o que esse enxame deixou, ainda outro comeu.

decisions.choice: four names for locusts: kinds of locust, stages of its growth, or simply four names for one plague
alternatives: four stages in the growth of one kind of locust
decisions.reason: The four words are the cutting locust (from a verb meaning to cut off), the swarming locust (the most common word for locust), the hopping or licking locust, and the stripping or finishing locust (from a verb meaning to consume). They may name different kinds of locust, or the stages through which a locust grows from a crawling young insect to a flying adult, or they may be four poetic names for the same insect. In 2:25 the four names come in a different order, which suggests that they are not a strict sequence. The point is plain either way: wave after wave came until nothing was left.

decisions.choice: a real locust plague, which stripped the land
decisions.reason: Swarms of desert locusts, in numbers beyond counting, can strip every green thing from a region in hours (Exodus 10:12-15). The law names locusts among the curses on a disobedient people (Deuteronomy 28:38, 42), and Solomon prays about them (1 Kings 8:37). The rest of the chapter describes the damage to vines, fig trees, grain and pasture. Some ancient readers took the four locusts as pictures of four enemy empires; the text itself speaks of locusts, which 1:6 and chapter 2 then describe as an invading army.

decisions.choice: the cutting locust, the swarming locust, the hopping locust, the stripping locust (L, B); one swarm of locusts after another (R)
decisions.reason: The names follow the wording set for the Twelve. Literal and Balanced give each name its own English word, so the reader can follow the chain and see it come back in 2:25. Readable does not name four kinds, which might settle a question the text leaves open (m1), and says what the chain means.

decisions.choice: "la langosta cortadora, la langosta migratoria, la langosta saltadora, la langosta devoradora" (L, B); "una nube de langostas tras otra" (R)
decisions.reason: The terms note's names for Joel's four locusts, each saying what its Hebrew name describes, so the chain can be followed here and recognized in 2:25. "Migratoria" for the common swarming locust (arbeh) is a first choice for a native reviewer. Readable does not name four kinds, as the English does not.

decisions.choice: "la sauterelle qui ronge, la sauterelle en essaim, la sauterelle qui bondit, la sauterelle qui dévaste" (L, B); "des nuées de sauterelles, l'une après l'autre" (R)
alternatives: le gazam, l'arbeh, le yéleq, le hasil
decisions.reason: The term sheet's names for Joel's four locusts, each describing what its Hebrew name says the insect does, since it is unsure whether they are kinds or stages; 2:25 repeats them in another order. Readable says one swarm after another, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "nzige wakataji, nzige wa makundi, nzige warukaji, nzige waharibifu" (L, B); "kundi moja la nzige baada ya jingine" (R)
decisions.reason: The term sheet's names, each saying what its Hebrew name describes (cutting, swarming, hopping, stripping) and kept clear of the Union Version's names; 2:25 repeats them in another order. Whether they are kinds or stages of locust is not known, so Readable does not name four kinds.

decisions.choice: "châu chấu cắn phá, châu chấu đàn, châu chấu non, cào cào ăn trụi" (L, B); "hết đàn châu chấu này đến đàn châu chấu khác" (R)
decisions.reason: The term sheet's names for Joel's four locusts, with "châu chấu non" as Psalm 105:34 and "cào cào ăn trụi" as 1 Kings 8:37; 2:25 repeats them in another order. Readable gives the sense, one swarm after another, without naming kinds the text leaves open.

decisions.choice: "자르는 메뚜기, 떼 지어 다니는 메뚜기, 뛰는 메뚜기, 갉아 먹는 메뚜기" (L, B); "메뚜기 떼가 잇달아" (R)
decisions.reason: The term sheet's names, each saying what its Hebrew name describes rather than the older Korean insect names, whose identifications are uncertain; 2:25 repeats them in another order. Readable says one swarm after another, as the English does.

decisions.choice: o gafanhoto cortador, o gafanhoto migrador, o gafanhoto saltador, o gafanhoto devorador (L, B); um enxame de gafanhotos depois do outro (R)
alternatives: a locusta, o gafanhoto, a lagarta, o pulgão
o cortador, o enxame, o saltador, o devorador
decisions.reason: For the whole book (the four names return in 2:25): as the English, each Hebrew name keeps one Portuguese word, so the reader can follow the chain. The cutter is "cortador"; the common swarming locust is "migrador", the name of the swarming kind that travels in clouds; the hopper is "saltador"; the one that finishes everything is "devorador". The old list "lagarta, pulgão" names other insects and hides that all four are locusts (m1). Readable does not name four kinds, as the English Readable.

source.text: הָקִ֤יצוּ שִׁכּוֹרִים֙ וּבְכ֔וּ וְהֵילִ֖לוּ כָּל־שֹׁ֣תֵי יָ֑יִן עַל־עָסִ֕יס כִּ֥י נִכְרַ֖ת מִפִּיכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Wake up, drunkards, and weep; and wail, all drinkers of wine, over [the] sweet wine, for it has been cut off from your mouth.

en.L: Wake up, drunkards, and weep; \q and wail, all drinkers of wine, \q over the sweet wine, for it is cut off from your mouth.
en.B: Wake up, you drunkards, and weep! \q Wail, all you who drink wine, \q because the sweet wine has been cut off from your lips.
en.R: Wake up, you drunkards, and cry! \q All you who drink wine, cry out in grief, \q because there is no more sweet wine for you to drink.

es.L: {{plural_you:Despierten|Despertad}}, borrachos, y {{plural_you:lloren|llorad}}; \q y {{plural_you:giman|gemid}}, todos los bebedores de vino, \q por el vino dulce, porque ha sido arrebatado de {{plural_you:su boca|vuestra boca}}.
es.B: ¡{{plural_you:Despierten|Despertad}}, borrachos, y {{plural_you:lloren|llorad}}! \q ¡{{plural_you:Giman|Gemid}}, todos los que beben vino, \q porque el vino dulce ha desaparecido de {{plural_you:sus labios|vuestros labios}}!
es.R: ¡{{plural_you:Despierten|Despertad}}, borrachos, y {{plural_you:lloren|llorad}}! \q Todos los que beben vino, ¡{{plural_you:lloren|llorad}} de dolor!, \q porque ya no queda vino dulce para beber.

fr.L: Réveillez-vous, ivrognes, et pleurez ; \q et lamentez-vous, vous tous, buveurs de vin, \q à cause du vin doux, car il est retranché de votre bouche.
fr.B: Réveillez-vous, ivrognes, et pleurez ! \q Lamentez-vous, vous tous qui buvez du vin, \q car le vin doux a été arraché à vos lèvres.
fr.R: Réveillez-vous, ivrognes, et pleurez ! \q Vous tous qui buvez du vin, criez de douleur, \q car il n’y a plus de vin doux à boire pour vous.

sw.L: Amkeni, enyi walevi, mlie; \q na ombolezeni, enyi nyote mnywao divai, \q kwa ajili ya divai tamu, kwa maana imekatiliwa mbali na vinywa vyenu.
sw.B: Amkeni, enyi walevi, mlie! \q Ombolezeni, enyi nyote mnaokunywa divai, \q kwa sababu divai tamu imeondolewa midomoni mwenu.
sw.R: Amkeni, enyi walevi, mlie! \q Enyi nyote mnaokunywa divai, lieni kwa huzuni, \q kwa sababu hakuna tena divai tamu ya kunywa.

vi.L: Hỡi những kẻ say rượu, hãy thức dậy và khóc lóc; \q hỡi tất cả những người uống rượu, hãy than khóc \q vì rượu ngọt, vì nó đã bị cất khỏi miệng các ngươi.
vi.B: Hỡi những kẻ say sưa, hãy tỉnh dậy mà khóc! \q Hỡi tất cả những người uống rượu, hãy gào khóc, \q vì rượu ngọt đã bị cất khỏi môi các ngươi!
vi.R: Hỡi những kẻ say rượu, hãy thức dậy mà khóc! \q Hỡi tất cả những người uống rượu, hãy kêu khóc đau thương, \q vì không còn rượu ngọt cho các ngươi uống nữa.

ko.L: 술 취한 자들아, 깨어 울어라. \q 포도주를 마시는 모든 자들아, 울부짖어라. \q 단 포도주 때문이다. 그것이 너희 입에서 끊어졌다.
ko.B: 술 취한 자들아, 깨어나 울어라! \q 포도주를 마시는 사람들아, 모두 통곡하여라! \q 단 포도주가 너희 입술에서 끊어졌다.
ko.R: 술 취한 자들아, 깨어나 울어라! \q 포도주를 마시는 사람들아, 모두 슬피 울어라! \q 너희가 마실 단 포도주가 더 이상 없다.

pt.L: Acordem, bêbados, e chorem; \q e lamentem, todos os bebedores de vinho, \q por causa do vinho doce, porque ele foi cortado da boca de vocês.
pt.B: Acordem, bêbados, e chorem! \q Gritem de dor, todos vocês que bebem vinho, \q porque o vinho doce foi tirado dos seus lábios.
pt.R: Acordem, bêbados, e chorem! \q Todos vocês que bebem vinho, gritem de tristeza, \q porque não há mais vinho doce para vocês beberem.

decisions.choice: sweet wine: the fresh juice of newly pressed grapes
decisions.reason: The word names new, sweet wine, the juice just trodden out of the grapes (Isaiah 49:26; Amos 9:13). With the vines stripped (verse 7) there will be no grape harvest. In 4:18 the same word returns in the promise that the mountains will drip with sweet wine.

decisions.choice: wake up, drunkards: the first to feel the loss are called to wake to the disaster
decisions.reason: The call to the drunkards has a bitter edge: they are told to wake from their stupor, and they are the first to notice that the wine is gone. The call to grieve then passes to the farmers (verse 11) and the priests (verse 13).

decisions.choice: Wail (L, B); cry out in grief (R); your lips (B)
decisions.reason: The call to wail follows the wording set in Isaiah: "Wail" at Literal and Balanced, "Cry out in grief" at Readable. Balanced says "lips" for "mouth"; Readable says plainly that the wine is gone.

decisions.choice: "giman" (L, B); "lloren de dolor" (R)
decisions.reason: The call to wail keeps the words of Spanish Isaiah 13:6, which Joel echoes in verse 15.

decisions.choice: "lamentez-vous" (L, B); "criez de douleur" (R)
decisions.reason: The call to wail keeps the words of the French Isaiah 13:6, which Joel quotes in verse 15.

decisions.choice: "ombolezeni" (L, B); "lieni kwa huzuni" (R)
decisions.reason: The call to wail keeps the words of the Swahili Isaiah 13:6, which Joel quotes in verse 15.

decisions.choice: "hãy than khóc" (L); "hãy gào khóc" (B); "hãy kêu khóc đau thương" (R)
decisions.reason: The call to wail keeps the words of the published Isaiah 13:6 at each level, the verse Joel quotes in verse 15.

decisions.choice: "울부짖어라" (L); "통곡하여라" (B); "슬피 울어라" (R)
decisions.reason: The call to wail keeps the words of the Korean Isaiah 13:6 at each level, the verse Joel quotes in verse 15.

decisions.choice: lamentem (L); gritem de dor (B); gritem de tristeza (R); o vinho doce
decisions.reason: For the whole book, the call to wail takes the words Isaiah 13:6 uses in Portuguese: "lamentem" (L), "gritem de dor" (B), "chorem e gritem de tristeza" shortened to "gritem de tristeza" (R), as the English follows Isaiah. The other mourning verbs (1:8, 1:13) take "prantear" and "chorar de luto" so the words stay apart. The fresh juice of m1 is "vinho doce" here and in 4:18.

records.literal_gloss: For a nation has come up against my land, mighty and without number; its teeth [are the] teeth of a lion, and [the] fangs of a lioness [are] to it.

en.L: For a nation has come up against {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} land, \q mighty and without number; \q its teeth [are] a lion's teeth, \q and it has the fangs of a lioness.
en.B: For a nation has invaded {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} land, \q powerful and too many to count. \q Its teeth are a lion's teeth; \q it has the fangs of a lioness.
en.R: A nation of locusts has invaded {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} land. \q It is powerful, and there are too many to count. \q Its teeth are like a lion's teeth. \q It has fangs like a lioness.

es.L: Porque una nación ha subido contra {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} tierra, \q poderosa y sin número; \q sus dientes [son] dientes de león, \q y tiene colmillos de leona.
es.B: Porque una nación ha invadido {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} tierra, \q poderosa e incontable. \q Sus dientes son dientes de león; \q tiene colmillos de leona.
es.R: Una nación de langostas ha invadido {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} tierra. \q Es poderosa, y son tantas que no se pueden contar. \q Sus dientes son como dientes de león. \q Tiene colmillos como los de una leona.

fr.L: Car une nation est montée contre {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} pays, \q puissante et sans nombre ; \q ses dents [sont] des dents de lion, \q et elle a des crocs de lionne.
fr.B: Car une nation a envahi {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} pays, \q puissante et innombrable. \q Ses dents sont des dents de lion ; \q elle a des crocs de lionne.
fr.R: Une nation de sauterelles a envahi {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} pays. \q Elle est puissante et trop nombreuse pour qu’on la compte. \q Ses dents sont comme des dents de lion. \q Elle a des crocs comme ceux d’une lionne.

sw.L: Kwa maana taifa limepanda juu ya nchi {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, \q lenye nguvu, lisilo na hesabu; \q meno yake [ni] meno ya simba, \q nalo lina magego ya simba jike.
sw.B: Kwa maana taifa limeivamia nchi {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, \q lenye nguvu na lisilohesabika. \q Meno yake ni meno ya simba; \q lina magego ya simba jike.
sw.R: Taifa la nzige limeivamia nchi {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}. \q Lina nguvu, na nzige wake ni wengi mno wasioweza kuhesabiwa. \q Meno yake ni kama meno ya simba. \q Lina magego kama ya simba jike.

vi.L: Vì một dân tộc đã kéo lên nghịch cùng đất của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, \q hùng mạnh và không đếm xuể; \q răng nó [là] răng sư tử, \q và nó có nanh của sư tử cái.
vi.B: Vì một dân tộc đã xâm chiếm đất của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, \q hùng mạnh và đông không đếm được. \q Răng nó là răng sư tử; \q nó có nanh của sư tử cái.
vi.R: Một dân tộc châu chấu đã xâm chiếm đất của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. \q Nó hùng mạnh, và đông đến nỗi không ai đếm được. \q Răng nó như răng sư tử. \q Nó có nanh như nanh sư tử cái.

ko.L: 한 민족이 내 땅을 치러 올라왔다. \q 강하고 수가 없는 민족이다. \q 그 이빨은 사자의 이빨이고, \q 그에게는 암사자의 송곳니가 있다.
ko.B: 한 민족이 내 땅을 침략했다. \q 강하고 셀 수 없이 많은 민족이다. \q 그 이빨은 사자의 이빨이고, \q 암사자의 송곳니를 가졌다.
ko.R: 메뚜기 떼가 한 민족처럼 내 땅을 쳐들어왔다. \q 그들은 힘이 세고, 너무 많아서 셀 수도 없다. \q 그 이빨은 사자의 이빨 같다. \q 암사자처럼 날카로운 송곳니를 가졌다.

pt.L: Pois uma nação subiu contra a {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} terra, \q poderosa e sem número; \q os seus dentes [são] dentes de leão, \q e ela tem as presas de uma leoa.
pt.B: Pois uma nação invadiu a {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} terra, \q poderosa e numerosa demais para se contar. \q Os seus dentes são dentes de leão; \q ela tem as presas de uma leoa.
pt.R: Uma nação de gafanhotos invadiu a {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} terra. \q Ela é poderosa, e são tantos que ninguém consegue contar. \q Os seus dentes são como dentes de leão. \q Ela tem presas como as de uma leoa.

decisions.choice: a nation: the locust swarm, pictured as an invading people
alternatives: a human army, foreshadowed by the locusts
decisions.reason: The word usually names a nation. Proverbs 30:25-27 calls ants and locusts "a people" in the same way. What this "nation" does in verse 7, stripping vines and fig trees, is what locusts do, so the swarm of verse 4 is meant, described as an army that invades the land. Chapter 2 develops the picture. Some readers take the nation as a human army that the locusts foreshadow.

decisions.choice: my land: the LORD speaks of the land as his own
alternatives: the prophet speaks for the people
decisions.reason: The speaker is not named. The land is called the LORD's land in 2:18 ("his land") and 4:2 ("my land"), and the vine and fig tree of verse 7 are "my" too, so the LORD most likely speaks here. The prophet may instead be speaking for the people, who would call it "my land" as well.

decisions.choice: teeth of a lion, fangs of a lioness: small insects that devour like the fiercest of animals
decisions.reason: Two words for the lion are used; the second may mean a lioness. A locust's jaws are tiny, but together the swarm devours as a lion tears its prey. Revelation 9:8 takes up the picture for its locusts.

decisions.choice: A nation of locusts
decisions.reason: Readable says that the nation is the locusts (m1), since a young reader would otherwise think of a human army.

source.text: שָׂ֤ם גַּפְנִי֙ לְשַׁמָּ֔ה וּתְאֵנָתִ֖י לִקְצָפָ֑ה חָשֹׂ֤ף חֲשָׂפָהּ֙ וְהִשְׁלִ֔יךְ הִלְבִּ֖ינוּ שָׂרִיגֶֽיהָ׃

records.literal_gloss: It has made my vine into a waste, and my fig tree into splinters; stripping it has stripped it and thrown [it] down; white have become its branches.

en.L: It has made {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} vine a waste \q and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} fig tree a splintered stump; \q it has stripped off its bark and thrown it down; \q its branches have turned white.
en.B: It has laid waste {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} vines \q and turned {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} fig trees to broken stumps. \q It has stripped off their bark and thrown it down, \q and their branches are left white.
en.R: It has ruined {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} grapevines \q and torn {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} fig trees to pieces. \q It has stripped off their bark and thrown it away. \q Now their branches are white and bare.

es.L: Ha hecho de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} vid una desolación, \q y de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} higuera un tocón astillado; \q le ha arrancado del todo la corteza y la ha tirado; \q sus ramas se han vuelto blancas.
es.B: Ha arrasado {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} viñas \q y ha dejado {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} higueras en tocones rotos. \q Les ha arrancado la corteza y la ha tirado, \q y sus ramas han quedado blancas.
es.R: Ha destruido {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} vides \q y ha hecho pedazos {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} higueras. \q Les ha arrancado la corteza y la ha tirado. \q Ahora sus ramas están blancas y desnudas.

fr.L: Elle a fait de {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} vigne une désolation \q et de {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} figuier un tronc brisé ; \q elle l’a entièrement écorcé et l’a jeté à terre ; \q ses branches sont devenues blanches.
fr.B: Elle a ravagé {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} vignes \q et réduit {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} figuiers en souches brisées. \q Elle en a arraché l’écorce et l’a jetée, \q et leurs branches sont restées toutes blanches.
fr.R: Elle a détruit {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} vignes \q et mis {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} figuiers en morceaux. \q Elle leur a arraché l’écorce et l’a jetée. \q Maintenant leurs branches sont blanches et nues.

sw.L: Limeufanya mzabibu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} kuwa ukiwa \q na mtini {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} kuwa kisiki kilichovunjika; \q limeubambua gome lake kabisa na kulitupa chini; \q matawi yake yamekuwa meupe.
sw.B: Limeiharibu mizabibu {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} \q na kuigeuza mitini {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} kuwa visiki vilivyovunjika. \q Limeibambua magome yake na kuyatupa, \q na matawi yake yamebaki meupe.
sw.R: Limeharibu mizabibu {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} \q na kuirarua mitini {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} vipande vipande. \q Limebambua magome yake na kuyatupa mbali. \q Sasa matawi yake ni meupe na matupu.

vi.L: Nó đã làm cho cây nho của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} thành hoang tàn \q và cây vả của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} thành gốc gãy vụn; \q nó đã lột sạch vỏ cây và quăng đi; \q các cành của nó đã trở nên trắng.
vi.B: Nó đã tàn phá các cây nho của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} \q và biến các cây vả của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} thành những gốc gãy. \q Nó đã lột vỏ cây và ném đi, \q để lại các cành trơ trắng.
vi.R: Nó đã phá hủy các cây nho của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} \q và xé nát các cây vả của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. \q Nó đã lột vỏ cây và ném đi. \q Giờ đây các cành cây trắng trơ trụi.

ko.L: 그것이 내 포도나무를 황폐하게 하고, \q 내 무화과나무를 부러진 그루터기로 만들었다. \q 그 껍질을 다 벗겨 던져 버리니, \q 그 가지들이 하얗게 되었다.
ko.B: 그것이 내 포도나무들을 망쳐 놓고, \q 내 무화과나무들을 부러진 그루터기로 만들었다. \q 껍질을 벗겨 던져 버리니, \q 가지들이 하얗게 드러났다.
ko.R: 그것이 내 포도나무들을 망가뜨리고, \q 내 무화과나무들을 갈기갈기 찢어 놓았다. \q 나무껍질을 벗겨 내던졌다. \q 이제 가지들이 하얗게 벌거벗었다.

pt.L: Ela fez da {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} videira uma desolação \q e da {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} figueira um toco lascado; \q descascou-a inteiramente e [a] lançou por terra; \q os seus ramos ficaram brancos.
pt.B: Ela devastou as {{deity_pronoun:minhas|Minhas}} videiras \q e reduziu as {{deity_pronoun:minhas|Minhas}} figueiras a tocos quebrados. \q Arrancou a casca delas e a jogou fora, \q e os seus ramos ficaram brancos.
pt.R: Ela destruiu as {{deity_pronoun:minhas|Minhas}} parreiras \q e despedaçou as {{deity_pronoun:minhas|Minhas}} figueiras. \q Arrancou a casca delas e a jogou longe. \q Agora os seus galhos estão brancos e nus.

decisions.choice: vine and fig tree: the main fruit crops, and a picture of the people's life in the land
decisions.reason: The vine and the fig tree stand for a settled, peaceful life in the land (1 Kings 5:5; Micah 4:4) and are sometimes pictures of Israel itself (Hosea 9:10). When the leaves and fruit are gone, locusts gnaw the bark, and the branches are left bare and white.

decisions.choice: a splintered stump: a rare word, perhaps for something snapped off
decisions.reason: The word is found only here. It comes from a root that may mean to snap or break off, so it pictures fig trees snapped and splintered, or perhaps their bark peeled into shreds.

decisions.choice: my vine, my fig tree: the LORD's, as in verse 6
decisions.reason: The "my" continues verse 6: the land and its vines and trees belong to the LORD (see the note there).

decisions.choice: vines, fig trees (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses the singular for the whole crop. Balanced and Readable use the plural, which says the same thing in natural English; Literal keeps the singular.

decisions.choice: a minha / as minhas with the deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: "Ela" in verses 6-7 is the nation, a feminine noun in Portuguese, so the swarm is "ela" where the English says "it". The possessive "minha(s)" agrees with the vine and fig trees and takes the deity_pronoun span, as the English "my" (m3).

source.text: אֱלִ֕י כִּבְתוּלָ֥ה חֲגֻֽרַת־שַׂ֖ק עַל־בַּ֥עַל נְעוּרֶֽיהָ׃

records.literal_gloss: Lament like a virgin girded [with] sackcloth for [the] husband of her youth.

en.L: Lament like a virgin wearing sackcloth \q for the husband of her youth.
en.B: Mourn like a young woman dressed in sackcloth, \q grieving for the man she was pledged to marry.
en.R: Cry like a young woman wearing sackcloth \q because the man she was going to marry has died.

es.L: Lamenta como virgen ceñida de cilicio \q por el esposo de su juventud.
es.B: Haz duelo como una joven vestida de cilicio \q que llora por el hombre con quien estaba comprometida.
es.R: Llora como una joven vestida con ropa áspera de luto \q porque ha muerto el hombre con quien se iba a casar.

fr.L: Lamente-toi comme une vierge vêtue d’un sac \q pour l’époux de sa jeunesse.
fr.B: Mène le deuil comme une jeune femme vêtue d’un sac, \q qui pleure l’homme qui lui était promis.
fr.R: Pleure comme une jeune femme en vêtements de deuil grossiers, \q parce que l’homme qu’elle allait épouser est mort.

sw.L: Omboleza kama bikira aliyejifunga nguo ya gunia \q kwa ajili ya mume wa ujana wake.
sw.B: Lia kwa huzuni kama msichana aliyevaa nguo ya gunia, \q anayemlilia mwanamume aliyekuwa amemchumbia.
sw.R: Lia kama msichana aliyevaa nguo ya gunia \q kwa sababu mwanamume aliyetarajia kumwoa amekufa.

vi.L: Hãy than van như trinh nữ thắt vải thô \q vì chồng thời xuân xanh của nàng.
vi.B: Hãy than khóc như một thiếu nữ mặc vải thô \q khóc thương người đàn ông nàng đã hứa hôn.
vi.R: Hãy khóc như một thiếu nữ mặc vải thô \q vì người đàn ông nàng sắp lấy làm chồng đã chết.

ko.L: 굵은 베를 두른 처녀가 \q 젊은 시절의 남편 때문에 [슬퍼하듯] 슬퍼하여라.
ko.B: 굵은 베옷을 입은 젊은 여자가 \q 약혼한 남자를 잃고 슬퍼하듯 슬퍼하여라.
ko.R: 거친 베옷을 입은 젊은 여자가 \q 결혼하려던 남자가 죽어서 울듯이 울어라.

pt.L: Pranteia como uma virgem cingida de pano de saco \q pelo marido da sua juventude.
pt.B: Chora de luto como uma moça vestida de pano de saco, \q que lamenta o noivo com quem ia se casar.
pt.R: Chora como uma moça vestida de pano de saco \q porque o homem com quem ela ia se casar morreu.

decisions.choice: lament: a command to one woman, the land or people pictured as a mourning bride
decisions.reason: The verb is a feminine singular command, and the word is found only here. The one addressed is not named: it is most likely the land, or Zion and its people, pictured as a woman in mourning.

decisions.choice: a virgin ... the husband of her youth: a young woman whose bridegroom has died before the marriage was complete
alternatives: a young wife mourning her husband
decisions.reason: The word for the woman names a young woman of marriageable age who has not yet married. In Israel a man pledged to marry a woman was already called her husband (Deuteronomy 22:23-24). So the picture is most likely of a young bride whose promised husband has died before the wedding. Others read it of a young wife whose husband has died.

decisions.choice: sackcloth: rough cloth worn in mourning
decisions.reason: Sackcloth was coarse cloth, often of goat's hair, worn next to the skin by those in mourning or in deep distress (Genesis 37:34; 2 Samuel 3:31).

decisions.choice: a young woman (B, R); the man she was pledged to marry (B); the man she was going to marry has died (R)
decisions.reason: Literal says "virgin" and "the husband of her youth". Balanced and Readable say what the picture means (m2). Readable says plainly that he has died, which the mourning implies.

decisions.choice: tú, singular command ("Lamenta", "Haz duelo", "Llora")
decisions.reason: The Hebrew command is feminine singular, addressed to the land or people pictured as a mourning bride (meaning decision), so Spanish uses tú with no plural_you span. "Cilicio" (L, B) and "ropa áspera de luto" (R) are the terms note's words for sackcloth.

decisions.choice: "tu" ("Lamente-toi", "Mène le deuil", "Pleure")
decisions.reason: The Hebrew command is feminine singular, addressed to the land or people pictured as a mourning bride (meaning decision), so French says "tu". Sackcloth is "sac" (L, B) and "vêtements de deuil grossiers" (R), as Jeremiah 4:8.

decisions.choice: singular "Omboleza" / "Lia"; "nguo ya gunia"
decisions.reason: The command is singular in the Hebrew, addressed to the land or people pictured as a mourning bride (meaning decision), and Swahili keeps the singular. Sackcloth is "nguo ya gunia", as Jeremiah 4:8.

decisions.choice: "trinh nữ" (L); "thiếu nữ" (B, R); "vải thô" for sackcloth
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "virgin"; Balanced and Readable say "young woman", as the English does, since the point is a bride not yet married (meaning decision). Sackcloth is "vải thô", as Jeremiah 4:8. The command has no pronoun, as Vietnamese imperatives allow.

decisions.choice: the comparison first, the command last ("…처녀가 … 슬퍼하듯 슬퍼하여라")
decisions.reason: Korean puts the verb at the end, so the picture of the mourning bride comes before the command; the line break keeps the Hebrew's two lines. Sackcloth is "굵은 베" (L), "굵은 베옷" (B) and "거친 베옷" (R), as Jeremiah 4:8.

decisions.choice: Pranteia (L); Chora de luto (B); Chora (R): singular "tu" imperative
decisions.reason: The command is to one woman, the land or Zion pictured as a mourning bride (m1), so Portuguese uses the singular imperative of "tu", as God's word does to Zion or a city addressed as one. "Pano de saco" is the sackcloth of Isaiah's Portuguese.

source.text: הָכְרַ֥ת מִנְחָ֛ה וָנֶ֖סֶךְ מִבֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה אָֽבְלוּ֙ הַכֹּ֣הֲנִ֔ים מְשָׁרְתֵ֖י יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Has been cut off grain offering and drink offering from [the] house of Yahweh; mourn the priests, ministers of Yahweh.

en.L: Grain offering and drink offering are cut off from the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; \q the priests mourn, \q the ministers of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: Grain offerings and drink offerings have ceased in the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q The priests grieve, \q those who serve {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: There is no more grain or wine to offer in the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q The priests who serve {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} are mourning.

es.L: Han sido cortadas la ofrenda de cereal y la libación de la casa {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}; \q están de luto los sacerdotes, \q los ministros {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}.
es.B: Las ofrendas de cereal y las libaciones han cesado en la casa {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}. \q Los sacerdotes se lamentan, \q los que sirven {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}.
es.R: Ya no hay cereal ni vino para ofrecer en el templo {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}. \q Los sacerdotes que sirven {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} están de luto.

fr.L: L’offrande de grain et la libation sont retranchées de la maison {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} ; \q les prêtres sont en deuil, \q les serviteurs {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}.
fr.B: Les offrandes de grain et les libations ont cessé dans la maison {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}. \q Les prêtres sont dans l’affliction, \q ceux qui servent {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.R: Il n’y a plus de grain ni de vin à offrir dans le temple {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}. \q Les prêtres qui servent {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} sont en deuil.

sw.L: Sadaka ya nafaka na sadaka ya kinywaji zimekatiliwa mbali na nyumba ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}; \q makuhani wanaomboleza, \q wahudumu wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.B: Sadaka za nafaka na sadaka za kinywaji zimekoma katika nyumba ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. \q Makuhani wanahuzunika, \q wale wanaomtumikia {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.R: Hakuna tena nafaka wala divai ya kutoa sadaka katika hekalu la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. \q Makuhani wanaomtumikia {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wanaomboleza.

vi.L: Tế lễ ngũ cốc và lễ quán đã bị cất khỏi nhà của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}; \q các thầy tế lễ than khóc, \q là những người phục vụ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}.
vi.B: Các tế lễ ngũ cốc và lễ quán đã ngưng trong nhà {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}. \q Các thầy tế lễ sầu não, \q là những người phục vụ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}.
vi.R: Không còn lúa hay rượu để dâng trong đền thờ của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}. \q Các thầy tế lễ phục vụ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đang than khóc.

ko.L: 곡식 제물과 부어 드리는 제물이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 집에서 끊어졌고, \q 제사장들, \q {{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 섬기는 자들이 슬퍼한다.
ko.B: 곡식 제물과 부어 드리는 제물이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 집에서 그쳤다. \q 제사장들이 애통한다. \q {{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 섬기는 사람들이 애통한다.
ko.R: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 성전에 바칠 곡식도 포도주도 더 이상 없다. \q {{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 섬기는 제사장들이 슬퍼한다.

pt.L: Foram cortadas a oferta de cereal e a oferta de bebida da casa {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}; \q os sacerdotes estão de luto, \q os ministros {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}.
pt.B: As ofertas de cereal e as ofertas de bebida cessaram na casa {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}. \q Os sacerdotes estão de luto, \q os que servem {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}.
pt.R: Não há mais cereal nem vinho para oferecer no templo {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}. \q Os sacerdotes que servem {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} estão de luto.

decisions.choice: grain offering and drink offering: the daily gifts offered with the morning and evening sacrifice
decisions.reason: Every morning and evening a lamb was offered with flour mixed with oil and with a drink offering of wine (Exodus 29:38-42; Numbers 28:3-8). With no grain, oil or wine, these daily offerings stop, and the regular worship of the temple is cut off.

decisions.choice: the house of the LORD: the temple in Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The temple is called the LORD's house throughout the Old Testament. Joel speaks of it as standing and in use (1:13-14, 16; 2:17).

decisions.choice: ministers of the LORD: those who serve him
decisions.reason: The word means those who serve or attend on someone. It is used for the priests and Levites who served at the altar (Exodus 28:43; Jeremiah 33:21).

decisions.choice: no more grain or wine to offer in the temple
decisions.reason: Readable says what the two offerings were made of, and "temple" for "the house of the LORD".

decisions.choice: a oferta de cereal, a oferta de bebida
decisions.reason: The two offerings (m1) take the Pentateuch's words (docs/pentateuch-portuguese-terms.md; Numbers 15:5): "oferta de cereal" and "oferta de bebida". "Libação" is the technical word, but few readers know it.

source.text: שֻׁדַּ֣ד שָׂדֶ֔ה אָבְלָ֖ה אֲדָמָ֑ה כִּ֚י שֻׁדַּ֣ד דָּגָ֔ן הוֹבִ֥ישׁ תִּיר֖וֹשׁ אֻמְלַ֥ל יִצְהָֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: Devastated [is the] field; mourns [the] ground; for devastated [is the] grain, dried up [the] new wine, fails [the] fresh oil.

en.L: The field is devastated; the ground mourns, \q for the grain is devastated, \q the new wine has dried up, the fresh oil fails.
en.B: The fields are laid waste; the ground is in mourning, \q for the grain is ruined, \q the new wine has dried up, and the olive oil has failed.
en.R: The fields are ruined, and the ground itself mourns. \q The grain is destroyed. \q There is no new wine and no olive oil.

es.L: El campo está devastado; la tierra está de luto, \q porque el grano está devastado, \q el mosto se ha secado, el aceite fresco desfallece.
es.B: Los campos están arrasados; el suelo está de luto, \q porque el grano se ha perdido, \q el vino nuevo se ha secado y el aceite de oliva se ha agotado.
es.R: Los campos están arruinados, y hasta la tierra está de luto. \q El grano está destruido. \q No hay vino nuevo ni aceite de oliva.

fr.L: Le champ est dévasté, le sol est en deuil, \q car le grain est dévasté, \q le vin nouveau est desséché, l’huile fraîche dépérit.
fr.B: Les champs sont ravagés, la terre est en deuil, \q car le grain est perdu, \q le vin nouveau s’est tari, et l’huile d’olive manque.
fr.R: Les champs sont ruinés, et la terre elle-même est en deuil. \q Le grain est détruit. \q Il n’y a plus de vin nouveau ni d’huile d’olive.

sw.L: Shamba limeharibiwa; ardhi inaomboleza, \q kwa maana nafaka imeharibiwa, \q divai mpya imekauka, mafuta mapya yamepunguka.
sw.B: Mashamba yameharibiwa; nchi iko katika maombolezo, \q kwa maana nafaka imeangamia, \q divai mpya imekauka, na mafuta ya zeituni yamekwisha.
sw.R: Mashamba yameharibika, na hata ardhi yenyewe inaomboleza. \q Nafaka imeharibiwa. \q Hakuna divai mpya wala mafuta ya zeituni.

vi.L: Đồng ruộng bị tàn phá; đất đai than khóc, \q vì lúa bị tàn phá, \q rượu mới đã khô cạn, dầu mới hao mòn.
vi.B: Đồng ruộng bị tàn phá; đất đai sầu thảm, \q vì lúa đã hư mất, \q rượu mới đã cạn, và dầu ô-liu không còn.
vi.R: Đồng ruộng bị hủy hoại, và chính đất đai cũng than khóc. \q Lúa bị tiêu hủy. \q Không còn rượu mới, cũng không còn dầu ô-liu.

ko.L: 밭이 황폐하고 땅이 슬퍼한다. \q 곡식이 황폐하고, \q 새 포도주가 말랐으며, 새 기름이 다했기 때문이다.
ko.B: 밭들이 황폐해지고 땅이 애곡한다. \q 곡식이 다 망가지고, \q 새 포도주가 말랐으며, 올리브기름도 떨어졌다.
ko.R: 밭들이 망가지고, 땅마저 슬퍼한다. \q 곡식이 다 없어졌다. \q 새 포도주도 없고 올리브기름도 없다.

pt.L: O campo está devastado; o solo está de luto, \q porque o cereal está devastado, \q o vinho novo secou, o azeite fresco definha.
pt.B: Os campos foram arrasados; a terra está de luto, \q porque o cereal foi destruído, \q o vinho novo secou, e o azeite acabou.
pt.R: Os campos estão arruinados, e a própria terra está de luto. \q O cereal foi destruído. \q Não há vinho novo nem azeite.

decisions.choice: the ground mourns: grieves, and also dries up
decisions.reason: Two Hebrew verbs sound the same: one means to mourn, the other to dry up. Here the ground "mourns" just after the priests mourn (verse 9), and the drying of the crops follows. The word may be chosen to carry both: the parched ground looks like a mourner.

decisions.choice: grain, new wine and fresh oil: the three great products of the land
decisions.reason: These are the gifts the LORD promised to a faithful people (Deuteronomy 7:13; 11:14), and their loss is among the curses of Deuteronomy 28:38-40, 51. Hosea 2:10-11 names the same three. "New wine" is freshly pressed wine; "fresh oil" is newly pressed olive oil. The Hebrew of the first line also plays on sound: "devastated" and "field" begin alike.

decisions.choice: olive oil (B, R); fresh oil (L)
decisions.reason: As in Hosea 2:10, Literal says "fresh oil" and Balanced and Readable "olive oil". Readable puts the three losses simply, and keeps "mourns" (m1).

decisions.choice: "el grano, el mosto, el aceite fresco" (L); "grano, vino nuevo, aceite de oliva" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The three harvests in the words Joel 2:19 and 2:24 use at each level, from Spanish Deuteronomy 11:14.

decisions.choice: "le grain, le vin nouveau, l'huile fraîche" (L); "l'huile d'olive" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The three harvests in the words Joel 2:19 and 2:24 use at each level, so the reader sees the losses of chapter 1 given back.

decisions.choice: "nafaka, divai mpya, mafuta mapya" (L); "mafuta ya zeituni" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The three harvests in the words Joel 2:19 and 2:24 use at each level.

decisions.choice: "lúa, rượu mới, dầu mới" (L); "dầu ô-liu" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The three harvests in the words Joel 2:19 and 2:24 use at each level.

decisions.choice: "곡식, 새 포도주, 새 기름" (L); "올리브기름" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The three harvests in the words Joel 2:19 and 2:24 use at each level, so the losses here are seen given back there.

decisions.choice: o azeite fresco (L); o azeite (B, R)
decisions.reason: Portuguese "azeite" already means olive oil, so Balanced and Readable say it in one word where the English says "olive oil"; Literal adds "fresco" for the freshly pressed oil, as Deuteronomy 11:14 names the same three gifts ("o teu cereal, o teu vinho novo e o teu azeite fresco"); this holds for 2:19 and 2:24.

source.text: הֹבִ֣ישׁוּ אִכָּרִ֗ים הֵילִ֨ילוּ֙ כֹּֽרְמִ֔ים עַל־חִטָּ֖ה וְעַל־שְׂעֹרָ֑ה כִּ֥י אָבַ֖ד קְצִ֥יר שָׂדֶֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Be ashamed, farmers; wail, vinedressers, over wheat and over barley; for has perished [the] harvest of [the] field.

en.L: Be ashamed, farmers; wail, vinedressers, \q over the wheat and over the barley, \q for the harvest of the field has perished.
en.B: Be dismayed, you farmers! Wail, you who tend the vines, \q over the wheat and the barley, \q because the harvest of the field is lost.
en.R: Farmers, be sad and dismayed! You who grow grapes, cry out in grief! \q Cry for the wheat and the barley, \q because the harvest in the fields is ruined.

es.L: {{plural_you:Avergüéncense|Avergonzaos}}, labradores; {{plural_you:giman|gemid}}, viñadores, \q por el trigo y por la cebada, \q porque ha perecido la cosecha del campo.
es.B: ¡{{plural_you:Queden|Quedad}} consternados, agricultores! ¡{{plural_you:Giman|Gemid}}, los que cuidan las viñas, \q por el trigo y la cebada, \q porque la cosecha del campo se ha perdido!
es.R: ¡Agricultores, {{plural_you:pónganse|poneos}} tristes y {{plural_you:desanímense|desanimaos}}! ¡Viñadores, {{plural_you:lloren|llorad}} de dolor! \q {{plural_you:Lloren|Llorad}} por el trigo y la cebada, \q porque la cosecha de los campos se ha arruinado.

fr.L: Soyez honteux, laboureurs ; lamentez-vous, vignerons, \q à cause du blé et de l’orge, \q car la moisson des champs a péri.
fr.B: Soyez consternés, cultivateurs ! Lamentez-vous, vous qui soignez les vignes, \q à cause du blé et de l’orge, \q car la récolte des champs est perdue.
fr.R: Cultivateurs, soyez tristes et consternés ! Vous qui cultivez la vigne, criez de douleur ! \q Pleurez sur le blé et sur l’orge, \q car la récolte des champs est ruinée.

sw.L: Oneni haya, enyi wakulima; ombolezeni, enyi watunza mizabibu, \q kwa ajili ya ngano na kwa ajili ya shayiri, \q kwa maana mavuno ya shamba yameangamia.
sw.B: Fadhaikeni, enyi wakulima! Ombolezeni, ninyi mnaotunza mizabibu, \q kwa ajili ya ngano na shayiri, \q kwa sababu mavuno ya shamba yamepotea.
sw.R: Enyi wakulima, huzunikeni na kufadhaika! Ninyi mnaolima mizabibu, lieni kwa huzuni! \q Lilieni ngano na shayiri, \q kwa sababu mavuno ya mashambani yameharibika.

vi.L: Hỡi những người làm ruộng, hãy hổ thẹn; hỡi những người trồng nho, hãy than khóc \q vì lúa mì và vì lúa mạch, \q vì mùa gặt ngoài đồng đã mất.
vi.B: Hỡi những người làm ruộng, hãy bối rối! Hỡi những người chăm sóc vườn nho, hãy gào khóc \q vì lúa mì và lúa mạch, \q vì mùa màng ngoài đồng đã mất hết.
vi.R: Hỡi những người làm ruộng, hãy buồn bã và thất vọng! Hỡi những người trồng nho, hãy kêu khóc đau thương! \q Hãy khóc vì lúa mì và lúa mạch, \q vì mùa màng ngoài đồng đã bị hủy hoại.

ko.L: 농부들아, 부끄러워하여라. 포도원 일꾼들아, 울부짖어라. \q 밀과 보리 때문이다. \q 밭의 추수가 망했기 때문이다.
ko.B: 농부들아, 낙심하여라! 포도원을 가꾸는 사람들아, 통곡하여라! \q 밀과 보리 때문에 통곡하여라. \q 밭의 수확이 사라졌다.
ko.R: 농부들아, 슬퍼하고 낙심하여라! 포도를 기르는 사람들아, 슬피 울어라! \q 밀과 보리를 생각하며 울어라. \q 밭의 수확이 다 망가졌다.

pt.L: Envergonhem-se, lavradores; lamentem, vinhateiros, \q pelo trigo e pela cevada, \q porque pereceu a colheita do campo.
pt.B: Fiquem consternados, agricultores! Gritem de dor, vocês que cuidam das videiras, \q pelo trigo e pela cevada, \q porque a colheita do campo se perdeu.
pt.R: Agricultores, fiquem tristes e desanimados! Vocês que plantam uvas, gritem de tristeza! \q Chorem pelo trigo e pela cevada, \q porque a colheita dos campos foi arruinada.

decisions.choice: be ashamed: be dismayed and disappointed, as when hope comes to nothing
decisions.reason: The verb is the usual one for shame. It is used of those whose hopes are disappointed (Jeremiah 14:3-4, of farmers in a drought). It sounds almost the same as the verb "dried up" in verses 10, 12 and 17, and the prophet plays on the two: the crops dry up and the farmers are put to shame.

decisions.choice: wheat and barley: the grain harvest
decisions.reason: Barley ripened first, in spring, and wheat some weeks later. Both are lost, so there is nothing to harvest at all.

decisions.choice: Be dismayed (B); be sad and dismayed (R); you who tend the vines (B); You who grow grapes (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "dismayed", the sense of "ashamed" here (m1), and describe the vinedressers' work.

decisions.choice: Envergonhem-se (L); Fiquem consternados (B); fiquem tristes e desanimados (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the verb of shame; Balanced and Readable say the sense here, hope come to nothing (m1). The sound play with "dried up" (verses 10, 12, 17) cannot be kept in Portuguese and is left to the meaning note.

source.text: הַגֶּ֣פֶן הוֹבִ֔ישָׁה וְהַתְּאֵנָ֖ה אֻמְלָ֑לָה רִמּ֞וֹן גַּם־תָּמָ֣ר וְתַפּ֗וּחַ כָּל־עֲצֵ֤י הַשָּׂדֶה֙ יָבֵ֔שׁוּ כִּֽי־הֹבִ֥ישׁ שָׂשׂ֖וֹן מִן־בְּנֵ֥י אָדָֽם׃ס

records.literal_gloss: The vine has dried up, and the fig tree withers; pomegranate, also palm, and apple tree, all [the] trees of the field have dried up; for has dried up joy from [the] children of mankind.

en.L: The vine has dried up, \q and the fig tree withers; \q pomegranate, palm also, and apple tree, all the trees of the field have dried up; \q indeed, joy has dried up from the children of mankind.
en.B: The vine has withered, \q the fig tree droops; \q pomegranate, palm, and apple tree, all the trees of the field are dried up. \q Surely joy has withered away from the people.
en.R: The grapevines are dry, \q and the fig trees are dying. \q The pomegranate trees, palm trees, apple trees, and all the trees in the fields have dried up. \q And the people have lost all their joy.

es.L: La vid se ha secado, \q y la higuera se marchita; \q el granado, también la palmera, y el manzano, todos los árboles del campo se han secado; \q ciertamente se ha secado el gozo de entre los hijos de los hombres.
es.B: La vid se ha marchitado, \q la higuera languidece; \q el granado, la palmera y el manzano, todos los árboles del campo están secos. \q Ciertamente la alegría se ha marchitado entre la gente.
es.R: Las vides están secas, \q y las higueras se están muriendo. \q Los granados, las palmeras, los manzanos y todos los árboles de los campos se han secado. \q Y la gente ha perdido toda su alegría.

fr.L: La vigne est desséchée, \q et le figuier dépérit ; \q le grenadier, le palmier aussi, et le pommier, tous les arbres des champs sont desséchés ; \q oui, la joie s’est desséchée chez les enfants des hommes.
fr.B: La vigne s’est flétrie, \q le figuier languit ; \q le grenadier, le palmier et le pommier, tous les arbres des champs sont secs. \q Oui, la joie s’est flétrie parmi le peuple.
fr.R: Les vignes sont sèches, \q et les figuiers meurent. \q Les grenadiers, les palmiers, les pommiers et tous les arbres des champs se sont desséchés. \q Et les gens ont perdu toute leur joie.

sw.L: Mzabibu umekauka, \q na mtini unanyauka; \q mkomamanga, mtende pia, na mtofaa, miti yote ya shambani imekauka; \q hakika furaha imekauka kutoka kwa wanadamu.
sw.B: Mzabibu umenyauka, \q mtini umedhoofika; \q mkomamanga, mtende na mtofaa, miti yote ya shambani imekauka. \q Hakika furaha imetoweka kati ya watu.
sw.R: Mizabibu imekauka, \q na mitini inakufa. \q Mikomamanga, mitende, mitofaa na miti yote ya mashambani imekauka. \q Na watu wamepoteza furaha yao yote.

vi.L: Cây nho đã khô héo, \q và cây vả tàn úa; \q cây lựu, cây chà là cũng vậy, và cây táo, mọi cây cối ngoài đồng đều đã khô héo; \q thật vậy, niềm vui đã khô héo khỏi con cái loài người.
vi.B: Cây nho đã héo, \q cây vả rũ xuống; \q cây lựu, cây chà là và cây táo, mọi cây cối ngoài đồng đều khô héo. \q Thật vậy, niềm vui đã héo tàn khỏi dân chúng.
vi.R: Các cây nho khô héo, \q và các cây vả đang chết dần. \q Cây lựu, cây chà là, cây táo và mọi cây cối ngoài đồng đều đã khô héo. \q Và dân chúng đã mất hết niềm vui.

ko.L: 포도나무가 말랐고, \q 무화과나무가 시들었다. \q 석류나무와 종려나무와 사과나무, 밭의 모든 나무가 말랐다. \q 참으로 사람의 자손들에게서 기쁨이 말라 버렸다.
ko.B: 포도나무가 시들고, \q 무화과나무가 축 늘어졌다. \q 석류나무, 종려나무, 사과나무, 밭의 모든 나무가 말라 버렸다. \q 참으로 백성에게서 기쁨이 시들어 버렸다.
ko.R: 포도나무들이 말랐고, \q 무화과나무들이 죽어 간다. \q 석류나무, 종려나무, 사과나무, 그리고 밭의 모든 나무가 말라 버렸다. \q 사람들은 기쁨을 모두 잃었다.

pt.L: A videira secou, \q e a figueira definha; \q romãzeira, também palmeira, e macieira, todas as árvores do campo secaram; \q sim, a alegria secou dentre os filhos da humanidade.
pt.B: A videira murchou, \q a figueira desfalece; \q a romãzeira, a palmeira e a macieira, todas as árvores do campo estão secas. \q De fato, a alegria murchou e se afastou do povo.
pt.R: As parreiras estão secas, \q e as figueiras estão morrendo. \q As romãzeiras, as palmeiras, as macieiras e todas as árvores dos campos secaram. \q E o povo perdeu toda a sua alegria.

decisions.choice: joy has dried up: the same verb as for the vine, with a play on "be ashamed"
decisions.reason: The verb used for the vine at the start of the verse is used again for joy at the end: the joy of the people withers with their trees. The same verb can be heard as "be put to shame" (see verse 11). Harvest was a time of great joy (Isaiah 9:2; 16:10), and now there is none.

decisions.choice: apple tree: perhaps another fruit tree, such as the apricot or quince
decisions.reason: The tree is named with the word for apple in later Hebrew, but it is not certain which fruit tree is meant in Bible times (Song of Songs 2:3; Proverbs 25:11).

decisions.choice: the children of mankind (L); the people (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew phrase, which means human beings. Balanced and Readable say "the people".

decisions.choice: "les enfants des hommes" (L)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew phrase for human beings with "enfants", which already includes women and keeps clear of "fils de l'homme", the Gospel title of Jesus.

decisions.choice: os filhos da humanidade (L)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew phrase for human beings with a word that includes everyone; the English has no gender span here, so neither does the Portuguese. The verb "secar" is used for the vine and for joy at Literal, keeping the repetition of m1.

source.text: חִגְר֨וּ וְסִפְד֜וּ הַכֹּהֲנִ֗ים הֵילִ֨ילוּ֙ מְשָׁרְתֵ֣י מִזְבֵּ֔חַ בֹּ֚אוּ לִ֣ינוּ בַשַּׂקִּ֔ים מְשָׁרְתֵ֖י אֱלֹהָ֑י כִּ֥י נִמְנַ֛ע מִבֵּ֥ית אֱלֹהֵיכֶ֖ם מִנְחָ֥ה וָנָֽסֶךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: Gird yourselves and lament, the priests; wail, ministers of [the] altar; come, spend the night in sackcloth, ministers of my God; for withheld from [the] house of your God [are] grain offering and drink offering.

en.L: Put on [sackcloth] and lament, you priests; \q wail, ministers of the altar; \q come, spend the night in sackcloth, ministers of my God! \q For grain offering and drink offering are withheld from the house of your God.
en.B: Put on sackcloth and mourn, you priests! \q Wail, you who serve at the altar! \q Come, spend the night in sackcloth, you who serve my God! \q For grain offerings and drink offerings are kept back from the house of your God.
en.R: Priests, put on sackcloth and mourn! \q You who serve at the altar, cry out in grief! \q You who serve my God, come and spend the night dressed in sackcloth. \q There is no grain or wine to offer in the temple of your God.

es.L: ¡{{plural_you:Cíñanse|Ceñíos}} [de cilicio] y {{plural_you:hagan|haced}} duelo, sacerdotes; \q {{plural_you:giman|gemid}}, ministros del altar; \q {{plural_you:vengan|venid}}, {{plural_you:pasen|pasad}} la noche en cilicio, ministros de mi Dios! \q Porque la ofrenda de cereal y la libación son retenidas de la casa de {{plural_you:su Dios|vuestro Dios}}.
es.B: ¡{{plural_you:Vístanse|Vestíos}} de cilicio y {{plural_you:hagan|haced}} duelo, sacerdotes! \q ¡{{plural_you:Giman|Gemid}}, los que sirven en el altar! \q ¡{{plural_you:Vengan|Venid}}, {{plural_you:pasen|pasad}} la noche vestidos de cilicio, los que sirven a mi Dios! \q Porque a la casa de {{plural_you:su Dios|vuestro Dios}} se le niegan las ofrendas de cereal y las libaciones.
es.R: ¡Sacerdotes, {{plural_you:vístanse|vestíos}} con ropa áspera de luto y {{plural_you:lloren|llorad}}! \q ¡Los que sirven en el altar, {{plural_you:lloren|llorad}} de dolor! \q Los que sirven a mi Dios, {{plural_you:vengan|venid}} y {{plural_you:pasen|pasad}} la noche vestidos con ropa áspera de luto. \q Ya no hay cereal ni vino para ofrecer en el templo de {{plural_you:su Dios|vuestro Dios}}.

fr.L: Ceignez-vous [de sacs] et menez le deuil, prêtres ; \q lamentez-vous, serviteurs de l’autel ; \q venez, passez la nuit vêtus de sacs, serviteurs de mon Dieu ! \q Car l’offrande de grain et la libation sont refusées à la maison de votre Dieu.
fr.B: Revêtez le sac et menez le deuil, prêtres ! \q Lamentez-vous, vous qui servez à l’autel ! \q Venez, passez la nuit vêtus de sacs, vous qui servez mon Dieu ! \q Car les offrandes de grain et les libations sont refusées à la maison de votre Dieu.
fr.R: Prêtres, mettez des vêtements de deuil grossiers et pleurez ! \q Vous qui servez à l’autel, criez de douleur ! \q Vous qui servez mon Dieu, venez passer la nuit en vêtements de deuil. \q Il n’y a plus de grain ni de vin à offrir dans le temple de votre Dieu.

sw.L: Jifungeni [nguo za magunia] mkaomboleze, enyi makuhani; \q pigeni yowe, enyi wahudumu wa madhabahu; \q njooni, lalini usiku katika nguo za magunia, enyi wahudumu wa Mungu wangu! \q Kwa maana sadaka ya nafaka na sadaka ya kinywaji zimezuiliwa mbali na nyumba ya Mungu wenu.
sw.B: Vaeni nguo za magunia mkaomboleze, enyi makuhani! \q Pigeni yowe, ninyi mnaohudumu madhabahuni! \q Njooni, mlale usiku mkiwa mmevaa nguo za magunia, ninyi mnaomtumikia Mungu wangu! \q Kwa maana sadaka za nafaka na sadaka za kinywaji zimenyimwa nyumba ya Mungu wenu.
sw.R: Enyi makuhani, vaeni nguo za magunia mkaomboleze! \q Ninyi mnaohudumu madhabahuni, lieni kwa huzuni! \q Ninyi mnaomtumikia Mungu wangu, njooni mlale usiku mkiwa mmevaa nguo za magunia. \q Hakuna tena nafaka wala divai ya kutoa sadaka katika hekalu la Mungu wenu.

vi.L: Hãy thắt [vải thô] và than van, hỡi các thầy tế lễ; \q hãy than khóc, hỡi những người phục vụ bàn thờ; \q hãy đến, nằm qua đêm trong vải thô, hỡi những người phục vụ Đức Chúa Trời của tôi! \q Vì tế lễ ngũ cốc và lễ quán đã bị cất khỏi nhà Đức Chúa Trời của các ngươi.
vi.B: Hỡi các thầy tế lễ, hãy mặc vải thô và than van! \q Hỡi những người phục vụ nơi bàn thờ, hãy gào khóc! \q Hỡi những người phục vụ Đức Chúa Trời của tôi, hãy đến mặc vải thô mà thức qua đêm! \q Vì tế lễ ngũ cốc và lễ quán đã bị khước từ khỏi nhà Đức Chúa Trời của các ngươi.
vi.R: Hỡi các thầy tế lễ, hãy mặc vải thô và than khóc! \q Hỡi những người phục vụ nơi bàn thờ, hãy kêu khóc đau thương! \q Hỡi những người phục vụ Đức Chúa Trời của tôi, hãy đến mặc vải thô suốt đêm. \q Không còn lúa hay rượu để dâng trong đền thờ của Đức Chúa Trời các ngươi.

ko.L: 제사장들아, [굵은 베를] 두르고 애곡하여라. \q 제단에서 섬기는 자들아, 울부짖어라. \q 내 하나님을 섬기는 자들아, 와서 굵은 베를 두르고 밤을 지내라! \q 곡식 제물과 부어 드리는 제물이 너희 하나님의 집에서 끊겼기 때문이다.
ko.B: 제사장들아, 굵은 베옷을 입고 애곡하여라! \q 제단에서 섬기는 사람들아, 통곡하여라! \q 내 하나님을 섬기는 사람들아, 와서 굵은 베옷을 입은 채 밤을 지새워라! \q 곡식 제물과 부어 드리는 제물이 너희 하나님의 집에 드려지지 못하고 있다.
ko.R: 제사장들아, 거친 베옷을 입고 슬퍼하여라! \q 제단에서 섬기는 사람들아, 슬피 울어라! \q 내 하나님을 섬기는 사람들아, 와서 거친 베옷을 입고 밤을 새워라. \q 너희 하나님의 성전에 바칠 곡식도 포도주도 없다.

pt.L: Cinjam-se [de pano de saco] e pranteiem, sacerdotes; \q lamentem, ministros do altar; \q venham, passem a noite em pano de saco, ministros do meu Deus! \q Porque a oferta de cereal e a oferta de bebida foram retidas da casa do Deus de vocês.
pt.B: Vistam pano de saco e chorem de luto, sacerdotes! \q Gritem de dor, vocês que servem no altar! \q Venham, passem a noite vestidos de pano de saco, vocês que servem o meu Deus! \q Pois as ofertas de cereal e as ofertas de bebida deixaram de chegar à casa do Deus de vocês.
pt.R: Sacerdotes, vistam pano de saco e chorem de luto! \q Vocês que servem no altar, gritem de tristeza! \q Vocês que servem o meu Deus, venham passar a noite vestidos de pano de saco. \q Não há cereal nem vinho para oferecer no templo do Deus de vocês.

decisions.choice: gird yourselves: put on sackcloth
decisions.reason: The verb means to tie something around the waist. Its object is left out, but it is clear from verse 8 and from the same verb in Isaiah 32:11 and Jeremiah 4:8: the priests are to put on sackcloth.

decisions.choice: spend the night in sackcloth: mourning without a break
decisions.reason: To keep on the sackcloth even through the night was a sign of deep and urgent grief, as when David pleaded for his child (2 Samuel 12:16) and Ahab humbled himself (1 Kings 21:27).

decisions.choice: my God ... your God: the prophet speaks, and the God he serves is theirs
decisions.reason: "My God" is the prophet's own, and "your God" is the priests'. The same God is meant: the prophet calls the priests to lead the people in turning to him.

decisions.choice: Put on [sackcloth] (L); Put on sackcloth (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal supplies "sackcloth" in brackets; Balanced and Readable supply it plainly (m1).

decisions.choice: o Deus de vocês
decisions.reason: "Seu Deus" could be read as "his God" beside "o meu Deus" (m3), so Portuguese says "o Deus de vocês" here and wherever the book says "your God" to the people.

source.text: קַדְּשׁוּ־צוֹם֙ קִרְא֣וּ עֲצָרָ֔ה אִסְפ֣וּ זְקֵנִ֗ים כֹּ֚ל יֹשְׁבֵ֣י הָאָ֔רֶץ בֵּ֖ית יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶ֑ם וְזַעֲק֖וּ אֶל־יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Consecrate a fast; call an assembly; gather [the] elders, all [the] inhabitants of the land, [to the] house of Yahweh your God, and cry out to Yahweh.

en.L: Set apart a fast; call a solemn assembly; \q gather the elders, all who live in the land, \q [to] the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, \q and to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} cry out.
en.B: Proclaim a holy fast; call a solemn assembly. \q Gather the elders and all who live in the land \q at the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, \q and cry to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for help.
en.R: Announce a holy fast, a time to go without food. Call everyone to a special meeting. \q Bring the elders and all the people of the land \q to the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, \q and cry out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for help.

es.L: {{plural_you:Consagren|Consagrad}} un ayuno, {{plural_you:convoquen|convocad}} una asamblea solemne; \q {{plural_you:reúnan|reunid}} a los ancianos, a todos los habitantes de la tierra, \q [en] la casa {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} {{plural_you:su Dios|vuestro Dios}}, \q y {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} {{plural_you:clamen|clamad}}.
es.B: {{plural_you:Proclamen|Proclamad}} un ayuno santo; {{plural_you:convoquen|convocad}} una asamblea solemne. \q {{plural_you:Reúnan|Reunid}} a los ancianos y a todos los que viven en el país \q en la casa {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} {{plural_you:su Dios|vuestro Dios}}, \q y {{plural_you:clamen|clamad}} {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} pidiendo ayuda.
es.R: {{plural_you:Anuncien|Anunciad}} un ayuno santo, un tiempo para no comer. {{plural_you:Llamen|Llamad}} a todos a una reunión especial. \q {{plural_you:Traigan|Traed}} a los ancianos y a toda la gente del país \q al templo {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} {{plural_you:su Dios|vuestro Dios}}, \q y {{plural_you:clamen|clamad}} {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} pidiendo ayuda.

fr.L: Consacrez un jeûne, convoquez une assemblée solennelle ; \q rassemblez les anciens, tous les habitants du pays, \q [dans] la maison {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} votre Dieu, \q et vers {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} criez.
fr.B: Proclamez un jeûne sacré, convoquez une assemblée solennelle. \q Rassemblez les anciens et tous les habitants du pays \q dans la maison {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} votre Dieu, \q et implorez le secours {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}.
fr.R: Annoncez un jeûne sacré, un temps où l’on se prive de nourriture. Appelez tout le monde à une réunion spéciale. \q Amenez les anciens et tous les gens du pays \q au temple {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} votre Dieu, \q et appelez {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} à l’aide.

sw.L: Takaseni mfungo; iteni mkutano mtakatifu; \q wakusanyeni wazee, wakaaji wote wa nchi, \q [katika] nyumba ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wenu, \q na kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} lieni.
sw.B: Tangazeni mfungo mtakatifu; iteni mkutano mtakatifu. \q Wakusanyeni wazee na wote wanaoishi katika nchi \q katika nyumba ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wenu, \q mkamlilie {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} awasaidie.
sw.R: Tangazeni mfungo mtakatifu, wakati wa kutokula chakula. Waiteni watu wote waje kwenye mkutano maalum. \q Waleteni wazee na watu wote wa nchi \q kwenye hekalu la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wenu, \q mkamlilie {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} awasaidie.

vi.L: Hãy biệt riêng một kỳ kiêng ăn; hãy triệu tập một buổi nhóm họp trọng thể; \q hãy nhóm các trưởng lão, mọi cư dân trong xứ, \q [vào] nhà {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của các ngươi, \q và hãy kêu cầu {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}.
vi.B: Hãy công bố một kỳ kiêng ăn thánh; hãy triệu tập một buổi nhóm họp trọng thể. \q Hãy nhóm các trưởng lão và mọi người sống trong xứ \q tại nhà {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của các ngươi, \q và kêu cầu {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} cứu giúp.
vi.R: Hãy công bố một kỳ kiêng ăn thánh, một thời gian nhịn ăn. Hãy kêu gọi mọi người đến một buổi họp đặc biệt. \q Hãy đưa các trưởng lão và toàn dân trong xứ \q đến đền thờ của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của các ngươi, \q và kêu cầu {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} giúp đỡ.

ko.L: 금식을 거룩하게 구별하고, 거룩한 모임을 소집하여라. \q 장로들과 그 땅의 모든 주민을 \q 너희 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 집으로 모으고, \q {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 부르짖어라.
ko.B: 거룩한 금식을 선포하고, 거룩한 모임을 소집하여라. \q 장로들과 그 땅에 사는 모든 사람을 \q 너희 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 집에 모으고, \q {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 도와 달라고 부르짖어라.
ko.R: 음식을 먹지 않는 거룩한 금식을 알려라. 모든 사람을 특별한 모임에 불러 모아라. \q 장로들과 그 땅의 모든 백성을 \q 너희 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 성전으로 데려오고, \q {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 도와 달라고 부르짖어라.

pt.L: Consagrem um jejum; convoquem uma reunião solene; \q reúnam os anciãos, todos os habitantes da terra, \q [na] casa {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}, o Deus de vocês, \q e {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}} clamem.
pt.B: Proclamem um jejum sagrado; convoquem uma reunião solene. \q Reúnam os anciãos e todos os que moram na terra \q na casa {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}, o Deus de vocês, \q e clamem {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}} por socorro.
pt.R: Anunciem um jejum sagrado, um tempo de ficar sem comer. Chamem todo mundo para uma reunião especial. \q Tragam os anciãos e todo o povo da terra \q ao templo {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}, o Deus de vocês, \q e clamem {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}} pedindo socorro.

decisions.choice: consecrate a fast, call a solemn assembly: a holy day of prayer for the whole people
decisions.reason: To "consecrate" a fast is to set it apart as a sacred act. A solemn assembly was a gathering of all the people for worship, on which no work was done (Leviticus 23:36). In time of danger the king or leaders proclaimed such a fast, as Jehoshaphat did when enemies invaded (2 Chronicles 20:3-4).

decisions.choice: gather the elders, all the inhabitants: the elders and the whole people are called together
decisions.reason: The Hebrew sets the two side by side without "and". They are most likely both gathered: the leaders and all the people (compare 2:16). The elders could instead be those who are told to gather everyone, "you elders, gather all the inhabitants".

decisions.choice: cry out: call for help in distress
decisions.reason: The verb is used for the cry of people in trouble to God (Exodus 2:23; Judges 3:9), the cry the prophet himself raises in verse 19.

decisions.choice: Proclaim a holy fast; call a solemn assembly (B); a time to go without food ... a special meeting (R)
decisions.reason: Readable explains what a fast and a solemn assembly were, and adds "for help" to "cry out" (m3). The same wording returns in 2:15.

decisions.choice: the wording of 2:15 at each level ("Consagren un ayuno, convoquen una asamblea solemne" L; "Proclamen un ayuno santo" B; "Anuncien un ayuno santo, un tiempo para no comer" R)
decisions.reason: Joel 2:15 repeats this call word for word, and the Spanish of both verses keeps one wording at each level.

decisions.choice: the wording of 2:15 at each level ("consacrez un jeûne, convoquez une assemblée solennelle" L; "Proclamez un jeûne sacré" B; "Annoncez un jeûne sacré, un temps où l'on se prive de nourriture" R)
decisions.reason: Joel 2:15 repeats this call, and French keeps one wording for it at each level.

decisions.choice: the wording of 2:15 at each level ("takaseni mfungo; iteni mkutano mtakatifu" L; "Tangazeni mfungo mtakatifu" B; "wakati wa kutokula chakula ... mkutano maalum" R)
decisions.reason: Joel 2:15 repeats this call, and Swahili keeps one wording for it at each level.

decisions.choice: the wording of 2:15 at each level ("hãy biệt riêng một kỳ kiêng ăn; hãy triệu tập một buổi nhóm họp trọng thể" L; "Hãy công bố một kỳ kiêng ăn thánh" B; "một thời gian nhịn ăn ... một buổi họp đặc biệt" R)
decisions.reason: Joel 2:15 repeats this call, and the Vietnamese keeps one wording for it at each level.

decisions.choice: the wording of 2:15 at each level ("금식을 거룩하게 구별하고, 거룩한 모임을 소집하여라" L; "거룩한 금식을 선포하고" B; "음식을 먹지 않는 거룩한 금식을 알려라" R)
decisions.reason: Joel 2:15 repeats this call, and Korean keeps one wording for it at each level, with "거룩한 모임" for the solemn assembly.

decisions.choice: uma reunião solene
decisions.reason: The solemn assembly (m1) is "reunião solene", the words Numbers 29:35 and Isaiah 1:13 use in Portuguese for the same Hebrew word; "assembleia" is kept for the people gathered (qahal, 2:16). The same wording returns in 2:15.

records.literal_gloss: Alas for the day! For near [is the] day of Yahweh, and like devastation from [the] Almighty it comes.

en.L: Alas for the day! \q For near [is] the day of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q and like destruction from [the] Almighty it will come.
en.B: Alas for that day! \q For the day of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is close at hand, \q and it will come like ruin from the Almighty.
