vi.R: Ngày ấy sẽ khủng khiếp biết bao! \q Ngày của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã gần! \q Ngày ấy sẽ đến như sự tàn phá do Đức Chúa Trời Toàn Năng sai đến.

ko.L: 아, 그날이여! \q {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 날이 가깝다. \q 전능하신 분에게서 오는 파멸같이 그날이 올 것이다.
ko.B: 아, 그날이 슬프다! \q {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 날이 가까이 왔다. \q 그날은 전능하신 분께서 보내시는 멸망처럼 올 것이다.
ko.R: 그날은 얼마나 끔찍할 것인가! \q {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 날이 가까이 왔다! \q 그날은 전능하신 하나님께서 보내시는 멸망처럼 올 것이다.

pt.L: Ai do dia! \q Porque perto [está] o dia {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}, \q e como destruição do Todo-Poderoso ele virá.
pt.B: Ai daquele dia! \q Porque o dia {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} está próximo, \q e ele virá como ruína enviada pelo Todo-Poderoso.
pt.R: Como aquele dia vai ser terrível! \q O dia {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} está perto! \q Ele virá como uma destruição enviada pelo Deus Todo-Poderoso.

decisions.choice: the day of the LORD: the day when the LORD comes to act in judgment, and to rescue
decisions.reason: The prophets speak of a coming day that belongs to the LORD, when he steps in to put down all that is proud and wicked (Isaiah 2:12; 13:6, 9; Zephaniah 1:14-18). Amos warns those who long for it that it will be darkness for Israel, not light (Amos 5:18-20). Joel speaks of it five times (1:15; 2:1, 11; 3:4; 4:14). Here the locust plague is a sign that the day is near. In chapter 2 it comes as the LORD's army against Zion; after the people turn back to him, it becomes the day when the LORD judges the nations and saves those who call on his name (3:4-5; 4:14-17). The New Testament takes up Joel's words for the day of the Lord (Acts 2:20).

decisions.choice: the same words as Isaiah 13:6
decisions.reason: "Near is the day of the LORD; like destruction from the Almighty it will come" is found word for word in Isaiah 13:6, against Babylon (compare Ezekiel 30:2-3; Obadiah 15; Zephaniah 1:7). In Hebrew "destruction" (shod) and "the Almighty" (Shaddai) sound alike. Joel turns words spoken against a foreign power toward his own people.

decisions.choice: alas for the day: a cry of dismay
decisions.reason: The cry is the one Jeremiah and Ezekiel raise before God in dismay (Jeremiah 1:6; Ezekiel 4:14). Here it is raised over the day itself, whether the day of the present disaster or the coming day of the LORD named in the next line.

decisions.choice: the wording of Isaiah 13:6 at each level; Alas for the day (L, B); How terrible that day will be (R)
decisions.reason: Where Joel repeats Isaiah 13:6, each level uses the wording already published there: "near [is] the day of the LORD ... like destruction from [the] Almighty" (L), "close at hand ... like ruin from the Almighty" (B), "is near ... like ruin sent by God All-Powerful" (R). Readable says "God All-Powerful" for Shaddai, as the Isaiah table sets, and gives the meaning of the cry "alas".

decisions.reason: Joel repeats Isaiah 13:6 word for word after his own cry, so each level reuses the published Spanish of that verse. "El día del SEÑOR" keeps one wording at every level through Joel.

decisions.reason: Joel repeats Isaiah 13:6 word for word after his own cry, so French reuses the published wording at each level; "le jour du SEIGNEUR" keeps one wording through Joel.

decisions.reason: Joel repeats Isaiah 13:6 word for word after his own cry, so each level reuses the published Swahili of that verse.

decisions.choice: "Ôi" for the cry (L, B); the published Isaiah 13:6 at each level ("ngày của CHÚA đã gần ... như sự hủy diệt từ Đấng Toàn Năng" L; "đã gần kề ... như sự tàn phá từ Đấng Toàn Năng" B; "do Đức Chúa Trời Toàn Năng sai đến" R)
decisions.reason: The cry is the one rendered "Ôi" in Jeremiah 1:6; "Than ôi" is kept for the 'ekhah of Lamentations. The rest of the verse repeats Isaiah 13:6 word for word, so each level reuses its published wording.

"O dia do SENHOR" is the book's phrase throughout, as in Isaiah and Ezekiel 13:5.

source.text: הֲל֛וֹא נֶ֥גֶד עֵינֵ֖ינוּ אֹ֣כֶל נִכְרָ֑ת מִבֵּ֥ית אֱלֹהֵ֖ינוּ שִׂמְחָ֥ה וָגִֽיל׃

records.literal_gloss: Is not before our eyes food cut off, from [the] house of our God joy and gladness?

en.L: Is not food cut off before our eyes, \q from the house of our God joy and gladness?
en.B: Has not the food been cut off before our very eyes, \q and joy and gladness from the house of our God?
en.R: We have watched our food disappear. \q There is no joy or celebration in the temple of our God.

es.L: ¿No ha sido cortado el alimento delante de nuestros ojos, \q de la casa de nuestro Dios la alegría y el regocijo?
es.B: ¿No ha desaparecido la comida ante nuestros propios ojos, \q y la alegría y el gozo de la casa de nuestro Dios?
es.R: Hemos visto cómo desaparecía nuestra comida. \q No hay alegría ni fiesta en el templo de nuestro Dios.

fr.L: La nourriture n’est-elle pas retranchée sous nos yeux, \q et de la maison de notre Dieu la joie et l’allégresse ?
fr.B: La nourriture n’a-t-elle pas disparu sous nos yeux mêmes, \q et la joie et l’allégresse de la maison de notre Dieu ?
fr.R: Nous avons vu disparaître notre nourriture. \q Il n’y a plus ni joie ni fête dans le temple de notre Dieu.

sw.L: Je, chakula hakijakatiliwa mbali mbele ya macho yetu, \q na furaha na shangwe kutoka nyumba ya Mungu wetu?
sw.B: Je, chakula hakijatoweka mbele ya macho yetu wenyewe, \q na furaha na shangwe kutoka nyumba ya Mungu wetu?
sw.R: Tumeona chakula chetu kikitoweka. \q Hakuna furaha wala sherehe katika hekalu la Mungu wetu.

vi.L: Chẳng phải lương thực đã bị cất khỏi trước mắt chúng ta, \q và khỏi nhà Đức Chúa Trời chúng ta niềm vui và sự hân hoan sao?
vi.B: Chẳng phải lương thực đã biến mất ngay trước mắt chúng ta, \q cùng niềm vui và sự hân hoan khỏi nhà Đức Chúa Trời chúng ta sao?
vi.R: Chúng ta đã thấy lương thực mình biến mất. \q Không còn niềm vui hay lễ hội trong đền thờ của Đức Chúa Trời chúng ta.

ko.L: 우리 눈앞에서 먹을 것이 끊어지지 않았느냐? \q 우리 하나님의 집에서 기쁨과 즐거움이 [끊어지지 않았느냐]?
ko.B: 바로 우리 눈앞에서 먹을 것이 없어지지 않았느냐? \q 우리 하나님의 집에서 기쁨과 즐거움이 사라지지 않았느냐?
ko.R: 우리는 먹을 것이 없어지는 것을 보았다. \q 우리 하나님의 성전에는 기쁨도 축제도 없다.

pt.L: Não foi cortado o alimento diante dos nossos olhos, \q da casa do nosso Deus a alegria e o júbilo?
pt.B: Não foi tirado o alimento diante dos nossos próprios olhos, \q e a alegria e o júbilo, da casa do nosso Deus?
pt.R: Nós vimos a nossa comida desaparecer. \q Não há alegria nem festa no templo do nosso Deus.

decisions.choice: joy and gladness in the house of God: the harvest festivals
decisions.reason: At the festivals of harvest the people brought the first and best of their crops to the temple, ate before the LORD and rejoiced (Deuteronomy 12:7; 16:10-15). With no harvest there are no offerings and no feast.

decisions.choice: is not ... cut off?: a question that expects the answer yes
decisions.reason: The question states what everyone can see. The prophet now speaks with the people ("our eyes", "our God").

decisions.choice: statements in place of the question (R)
decisions.reason: Readable turns the question into two plain statements, which say the same thing.

source.text: עָבְשׁ֣וּ פְרֻד֗וֹת תַּ֚חַת מֶגְרְפֹ֣תֵיהֶ֔ם נָשַׁ֨מּוּ֙ אֹֽצָר֔וֹת נֶהֶרְס֖וּ מַמְּגֻר֑וֹת כִּ֥י הֹבִ֖ישׁ דָּגָֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: Have shriveled [the] seeds under their clods; desolate [are the] storehouses; torn down [are the] granaries; for has dried up [the] grain.

en.L: The seeds have shriveled under their clods; \q the storehouses are desolate; \q the granaries are torn down, \q for the grain has dried up.
en.B: The seeds lie shriveled under the clods; \q the storehouses stand empty; \q the granaries are falling down, \q for the grain has withered.
en.R: The seeds have dried up in the ground. \q The storehouses are empty. \q The barns are falling down, \q because there is no grain.

es.L: Se han resecado las semillas bajo sus terrones; \q los almacenes están desolados; \q los graneros están derribados, \q porque se ha secado el grano.
es.B: Las semillas yacen resecas bajo los terrones; \q los almacenes están vacíos; \q los graneros se derrumban, \q porque el grano se ha marchitado.
es.R: Las semillas se han secado en la tierra. \q Los almacenes están vacíos. \q Los graneros se están cayendo, \q porque no hay grano.

fr.L: Les semences se sont desséchées sous leurs mottes ; \q les entrepôts sont désolés ; \q les greniers sont démolis, \q car le grain s’est desséché.
fr.B: Les semences gisent desséchées sous les mottes ; \q les entrepôts restent vides ; \q les greniers tombent en ruine, \q car le grain s’est flétri.
fr.R: Les semences ont séché dans la terre. \q Les entrepôts sont vides. \q Les granges s’écroulent, \q car il n’y a pas de grain.

sw.L: Mbegu zimesinyaa chini ya madongoa yake; \q ghala zimekuwa ukiwa; \q vihenge vimebomolewa, \q kwa maana nafaka imekauka.
sw.B: Mbegu zimesinyaa chini ya madongoa; \q ghala ziko tupu; \q vihenge vinaanguka, \q kwa maana nafaka imenyauka.
sw.R: Mbegu zimekauka ardhini. \q Ghala ziko tupu. \q Vihenge vinabomoka, \q kwa sababu hakuna nafaka.

vi.L: Hạt giống đã teo khô dưới các cục đất; \q các kho tàng bị bỏ hoang; \q các vựa lúa bị phá đổ, \q vì lúa đã khô héo.
vi.B: Hạt giống nằm khô héo dưới các cục đất; \q các kho trống không; \q các vựa lúa sụp đổ, \q vì lúa đã héo tàn.
vi.R: Hạt giống đã khô trong lòng đất. \q Các kho trống rỗng. \q Các vựa lúa đổ nát, \q vì không có lúa.

ko.L: 씨앗들이 흙덩이 아래에서 말라 쪼그라들었고, \q 곳간들이 황폐하며, \q 창고들이 무너졌다. \q 곡식이 말랐기 때문이다.
ko.B: 씨앗들이 흙덩이 아래에서 말라 버렸고, \q 곳간들은 텅 비었으며, \q 창고들은 무너져 내린다. \q 곡식이 시들었기 때문이다.
ko.R: 씨앗들이 땅속에서 말라 버렸다. \q 곳간들이 텅 비었다. \q 창고들이 무너지고 있다. \q 곡식이 없기 때문이다.

pt.L: As sementes murcharam debaixo dos seus torrões; \q os armazéns estão desolados; \q os celeiros estão derrubados, \q porque o cereal secou.
pt.B: As sementes estão murchas debaixo dos torrões; \q os armazéns estão vazios; \q os celeiros estão caindo, \q porque o cereal murchou.
pt.R: As sementes secaram debaixo da terra. \q Os armazéns estão vazios. \q Os celeiros estão caindo aos pedaços, \q porque não há cereal.

decisions.choice: the seeds have shriveled under their clods: three rare words, and an uncertain line
alternatives: a reading of the Greek: heifers stamping at their stalls
decisions.reason: The verb, the word for "seeds" and the word for "clods" are each found only here. The reading followed takes them as the sown seed drying up in the parched ground before it can sprout. The ancient translations understood the line very differently; the Greek translation, for example, speaks of heifers stamping at their stalls. The general sense, that the drought kills the crop before it grows, fits the verses around it.

decisions.choice: desolate storehouses, torn-down granaries: no grain to store, so the buildings fall into ruin
decisions.reason: With no harvest to put in them, the storehouses stand empty and the granaries are left to fall down. The last line repeats the play on the verb "dry up" and "be ashamed" (verses 10-12).

decisions.choice: barns (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says "barns" for granaries.

source.text: מַה־נֶּאֶנְחָ֣ה בְהֵמָ֗ה נָבֹ֨כוּ֙ עֶדְרֵ֣י בָקָ֔ר כִּ֛י אֵ֥ין מִרְעֶ֖ה לָהֶ֑ם גַּם־עֶדְרֵ֥י הַצֹּ֖אן נֶאְשָֽׁמוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: How groan [the] beasts! Wander in confusion [the] herds of cattle, for there is no pasture for them; even the flocks of sheep suffer punishment.

en.L: How the animals groan! The herds of cattle wander in confusion, \q for there is no pasture for them; \q even the flocks of sheep suffer.
en.B: How the animals moan! The herds of cattle wander about in confusion, \q because they have no pasture; \q the flocks of sheep are suffering as well.
en.R: Listen to the animals groan! The cattle wander around, confused, \q because they have no grass to eat. \q Even the sheep are suffering.

es.L: ¡Cómo gimen las bestias! Andan desconcertadas las manadas de ganado, \q porque no hay pasto para ellas; \q también los rebaños de ovejas sufren.
es.B: ¡Cómo braman los animales! Las manadas de ganado vagan sin rumbo, \q porque no tienen pastos; \q también los rebaños de ovejas sufren.
es.R: ¡{{plural_you:Oigan|Oíd}} cómo gimen los animales! El ganado anda de un lado a otro, confundido, \q porque no tiene hierba que comer. \q Hasta las ovejas están sufriendo.

fr.L: Comme les bêtes gémissent ! Les troupeaux de bœufs errent éperdus, \q car il n’y a pas de pâturage pour eux ; \q même les troupeaux de brebis souffrent.
fr.B: Comme les animaux mugissent ! Les troupeaux de bœufs errent, désorientés, \q parce qu’ils n’ont pas de pâturage ; \q les troupeaux de brebis souffrent eux aussi.
fr.R: Écoutez gémir les animaux ! Le bétail erre, perdu, \q parce qu’il n’a pas d’herbe à manger. \q Même les moutons souffrent.

sw.L: Jinsi wanyama wanavyolia kwa uchungu! Makundi ya ng'ombe yanatangatanga kwa fadhaa, \q kwa maana hakuna malisho kwa ajili yao; \q hata makundi ya kondoo yanateseka.
sw.B: Jinsi wanyama wanavyopiga kite! Makundi ya ng'ombe yanazunguka bila kujua pa kwenda, \q kwa sababu hayana malisho; \q makundi ya kondoo nayo yanateseka.
sw.R: Sikilizeni wanyama wanavyolia! Ng'ombe wanatangatanga, wamechanganyikiwa, \q kwa sababu hawana majani ya kula. \q Hata kondoo wanateseka.

vi.L: Súc vật rên siết biết bao! Các bầy bò đi lang thang bối rối, \q vì không có đồng cỏ cho chúng; \q ngay cả các bầy chiên cũng chịu khổ.
vi.B: Súc vật rên rỉ biết bao! Các đàn bò đi quanh quẩn hoang mang, \q vì chúng không có đồng cỏ; \q các bầy chiên cũng chịu khổ.
vi.R: Hãy nghe súc vật rên rỉ! Bò đi lang thang, ngơ ngác, \q vì không có cỏ để ăn. \q Ngay cả chiên cũng chịu khổ.

ko.L: 짐승들이 어찌나 신음하는지! 소 떼가 갈 바를 몰라 헤맨다. \q 그들에게 꼴이 없기 때문이다. \q 양 떼까지도 고통을 겪는다.
ko.B: 가축들이 얼마나 울부짖는가! 소 떼가 어쩔 줄 몰라 헤맨다. \q 풀밭이 없기 때문이다. \q 양 떼도 고통을 당한다.
ko.R: 짐승들이 신음하는 소리를 들어 보아라! 소들이 갈팡질팡 헤맨다. \q 먹을 풀이 없기 때문이다. \q 양들까지도 고통을 겪고 있다.

pt.L: Como gemem os animais! Os rebanhos de gado vagueiam confusos, \q porque não há pasto para eles; \q até os rebanhos de ovelhas sofrem.
pt.B: Como gemem os animais! Os rebanhos de bois andam sem rumo, confusos, \q porque não têm pasto; \q os rebanhos de ovelhas também estão sofrendo.
pt.R: Ouçam os animais gemendo! O gado anda de um lado para o outro, confuso, \q porque não tem capim para comer. \q Até as ovelhas estão sofrendo.

decisions.choice: suffer: bear the punishment of the land
decisions.reason: The verb usually means to bear guilt and its punishment. The animals have done no wrong, but they share in the punishment that falls on the land (Jeremiah 14:5-6; Hosea 4:3). A verb with almost the same letters means "be desolate", and some ancient translations read it that way.

decisions.choice: the animals: domestic herds and flocks with nothing to graze
decisions.reason: Cattle and sheep depended on open pasture. With the grass gone they wander in search of food. Their groaning joins the people's lament, as the wild animals' longing does in verse 20.

decisions.choice: Listen to (R); no grass to eat (R)
decisions.reason: Readable puts the exclamation "How ...!" as a call to listen, and says what pasture is.

source.text: אֵלֶ֥יךָ יְהוָ֖ה אֶקְרָ֑א כִּ֣י אֵ֗שׁ אָֽכְלָה֙ נְא֣וֹת מִדְבָּ֔ר וְלֶ֣הָבָ֔ה לִהֲטָ֖ה כָּל־עֲצֵ֥י הַשָּׂדֶֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: To you, Yahweh, I call; for fire has consumed [the] pastures of [the] wilderness, and a flame has set ablaze all [the] trees of the field.

en.L: To {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, I call, \q for fire has consumed the pastures of the wilderness, \q and flame has burned up all the trees of the field.
en.B: To {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, I cry out, \q for fire has devoured the pastures in the wilderness, \q and flames have burned up all the trees of the field.
en.R: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, I am calling out to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} for help. \q Fire has burned up the grasslands, \q and flames have burned all the trees in the fields.

es.L: A {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}, {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, clamo, \q porque el fuego ha consumido los pastos del desierto, \q y la llama ha abrasado todos los árboles del campo.
es.B: A {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}} clamo, {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, \q porque el fuego ha devorado los pastos del desierto, \q y las llamas han quemado todos los árboles del campo.
es.R: {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, a {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}} clamo pidiendo ayuda. \q El fuego ha quemado los pastizales, \q y las llamas han quemado todos los árboles de los campos.

fr.L: Vers {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}, {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, je crie, \q car le feu a dévoré les pâturages du désert, \q et la flamme a embrasé tous les arbres des champs.
fr.B: C’est vers {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}, {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, que je crie, \q car le feu a dévoré les pâturages du désert, \q et les flammes ont consumé tous les arbres des champs.
fr.R: {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, c’est {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} que j’appelle à l’aide. \q Le feu a brûlé les prairies, \q et les flammes ont brûlé tous les arbres des champs.

sw.L: Kwako {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}}, Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, ninaita, \q kwa maana moto umeteketeza malisho ya nyikani, \q na mwali wa moto umeiunguza miti yote ya shambani.
sw.B: Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, ninakulilia {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}}, \q kwa maana moto umeyateketeza malisho ya nyikani, \q na miali ya moto imeiunguza miti yote ya shambani.
sw.R: Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, ninakuita {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} unisaidie. \q Moto umeteketeza nyanda za majani, \q na miali ya moto imeiunguza miti yote ya mashambani.

vi.L: Lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, con kêu cầu {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, \q vì lửa đã thiêu nuốt các đồng cỏ nơi hoang mạc, \q và ngọn lửa đã đốt cháy mọi cây cối ngoài đồng.
vi.B: Lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, con kêu van {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, \q vì lửa đã thiêu nuốt các đồng cỏ nơi hoang mạc, \q và lửa ngọn đã thiêu rụi mọi cây cối ngoài đồng.
vi.R: Lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, con kêu xin {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} giúp đỡ. \q Lửa đã thiêu rụi các đồng cỏ, \q và ngọn lửa đã đốt cháy mọi cây cối ngoài đồng.

ko.L: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, 제가 주님께 부르짖습니다. \q 불이 광야의 목초지를 삼켰고, \q 불꽃이 밭의 모든 나무를 태웠기 때문입니다.
ko.B: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, 제가 주님께 울부짖습니다. \q 불이 광야의 풀밭을 삼켜 버렸고, \q 불꽃이 들의 모든 나무를 살라 버렸습니다.
ko.R: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, 제가 주님께 도와 달라고 부르짖습니다. \q 불이 풀밭을 다 태워 버렸고, \q 불꽃이 밭의 나무를 모두 태워 버렸습니다.

pt.L: A {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}, {{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}}, eu clamo, \q porque o fogo consumiu as pastagens do deserto, \q e a chama queimou todas as árvores do campo.
pt.B: A {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}, {{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}}, eu clamo, \q pois o fogo devorou as pastagens do deserto, \q e as chamas queimaram todas as árvores do campo.
pt.R: {{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}}, eu estou clamando a {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}} por socorro. \q O fogo queimou os campos de pasto, \q e as chamas queimaram todas as árvores dos campos.

decisions.choice: I call to you, LORD: the prophet's own prayer
decisions.reason: The prophet now prays in his own voice, crying out to the LORD as he told the people to do (verse 14). His prayer closes the chapter.

decisions.choice: fire ... the pastures of the wilderness: drought and heat that scorch the land like fire
decisions.reason: The "wilderness" here is the open, uncultivated country used for grazing, not desert. The fire may be the burning heat of drought, which leaves the land as if burned, and grass fires in the dry fields may be meant as well. In 2:3 the locust army is also pictured as fire.

decisions.choice: LORD with no "O"
decisions.reason: The divine name spoken to God is written with no "O", as in the Psalms and the other prophets. Readable says "for help", the sense of the cry.

decisions.choice: tú to the LORD, vocative "SEÑOR" with no "oh"
decisions.reason: The prophet's own prayer speaks to God with tú, as the prayers of the Spanish Psalms and prophets do; the vocative divine name takes no article and no "oh" (terms note).

decisions.choice: "tu" to the LORD; vocative "SEIGNEUR" with no "ô"
decisions.reason: The prophet's own prayer, as the Psalms in French: "tu" to God, and the vocative divine name without article or "ô" (term sheet). The past tenses of the prayer are passé composé.

decisions.choice: "Ee BWANA"; span on the free pronoun "wewe" only
decisions.reason: The prophet's prayer takes the vocative "Ee BWANA", as the Isaiah note settles. The object marker "-ku-" in "ninakulilia" cannot take a capital, so the deity_pronoun span stands only on the free pronoun "wewe".

decisions.choice: "Lạy CHÚA" first; the prophet says "con" and calls God "Ngài"
decisions.reason: Vietnamese puts the address at the head of a prayer, so "Lạy CHÚA" comes before "to you"; a prophet praying says "con" to God, as the address note for the Twelve sets.

decisions.choice: 합쇼체 with "저", addressing God as "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}여" and "주님"
decisions.reason: The prophet turns from calling the people (해라체) to his own prayer, which is 합쇼체, as prayers in the prophets are; the vocative divine name comes first, as Korean prayers begin.

decisions.choice: A ti, SENHOR, eu clamo: "tu" to God, and the name with no article
decisions.reason: The prophet prays, so he speaks to God with "tu" (docs/portuguese-style.md, section 4); in the vocative the divine name has no article, "SENHOR" alone, as the English writes "LORD" with no "O".

decisions.choice: as pastagens do deserto (L, B); os campos de pasto (R)
decisions.reason: The open grazing country (m2) is "deserto", the terms list's word for the wilderness, which in biblical Portuguese covers land that is not farmed; Readable says plainly "campos de pasto", as the English "grasslands".

source.text: גַּם־בַּהֲמ֥וֹת שָׂדֶ֖ה תַּעֲר֣וֹג אֵלֶ֑יךָ כִּ֤י יָֽבְשׁוּ֙ אֲפִ֣יקֵי מָ֔יִם וְאֵ֕שׁ אָכְלָ֖ה נְא֥וֹת הַמִּדְבָּֽר׃פ

records.literal_gloss: Even [the] animals of [the] field pant for you; for have dried up [the] channels of water, and fire has consumed the pastures of the wilderness.

en.L: Even the animals of the field pant for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, \q for the channels of water are dried up, \q and fire has consumed the pastures of the wilderness.
en.B: Even the wild animals long for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, \q because the streams of water have dried up, \q and fire has devoured the pastures in the wilderness.
en.R: Even the wild animals cry out to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, \q because the streams have dried up, \q and fire has burned up the grasslands.

es.L: Aun los animales del campo jadean por {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}, \q porque se han secado los cauces de las aguas, \q y el fuego ha consumido los pastos del desierto.
es.B: Hasta los animales salvajes suspiran por {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}, \q porque las corrientes de agua se han secado, \q y el fuego ha devorado los pastos del desierto.
es.R: Hasta los animales salvajes claman a {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}, \q porque los arroyos se han secado, \q y el fuego ha quemado los pastizales.

fr.L: Même les bêtes des champs soupirent après {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}, \q car les cours d’eau sont à sec, \q et le feu a dévoré les pâturages du désert.
fr.B: Même les animaux sauvages languissent après {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}, \q car les ruisseaux se sont asséchés, \q et le feu a dévoré les pâturages du désert.
fr.R: Même les animaux sauvages crient vers {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}, \q car les ruisseaux sont à sec, \q et le feu a brûlé les prairies.

sw.L: Hata wanyama wa shambani wanahema wakikutamani {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}}, \q kwa maana mifereji ya maji imekauka, \q na moto umeteketeza malisho ya nyikani.
sw.B: Hata wanyama wa porini wanakutamani {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}}, \q kwa sababu vijito vya maji vimekauka, \q na moto umeyateketeza malisho ya nyikani.
sw.R: Hata wanyama wa porini wanakulilia {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}}, \q kwa sababu vijito vimekauka, \q na moto umeteketeza nyanda za majani.

vi.L: Ngay cả các thú đồng cũng thở hổn hển hướng về {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, \q vì các dòng nước đã khô cạn, \q và lửa đã thiêu nuốt các đồng cỏ nơi hoang mạc.
vi.B: Ngay cả các loài thú hoang cũng khao khát {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, \q vì các dòng suối đã cạn khô, \q và lửa đã thiêu nuốt các đồng cỏ nơi hoang mạc.
vi.R: Ngay cả các loài thú hoang cũng kêu cầu {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, \q vì các dòng suối đã khô cạn, \q và lửa đã thiêu rụi các đồng cỏ.

ko.L: 들의 짐승들까지도 주님을 향하여 헐떡입니다. \q 물줄기들이 말랐고, \q 불이 광야의 목초지를 삼켰기 때문입니다.
ko.B: 들짐승들도 주님을 애타게 찾습니다. \q 시냇물이 말라 버렸고, \q 불이 광야의 풀밭을 삼켜 버렸기 때문입니다.
ko.R: 들짐승들까지도 주님께 부르짖습니다. \q 시냇물이 말라 버렸고, \q 불이 풀밭을 다 태워 버렸습니다.

pt.L: Até os animais do campo bramam por {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}, \q porque secaram os canais de água, \q e o fogo consumiu as pastagens do deserto.
pt.B: Até os animais selvagens anseiam por {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}, \q porque os riachos secaram, \q e o fogo devorou as pastagens do deserto.
pt.R: Até os animais selvagens clamam a {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}, \q porque os riachos secaram, \q e o fogo queimou os campos de pasto.

decisions.choice: pant for you: the longing of a thirsty animal
decisions.reason: The same verb is used in Psalm 42:2: "As a deer pants for streams of water, so my soul pants for you, God." Here the wild animals, finding the streams dry, look to God for water.

decisions.choice: fire has consumed the pastures of the wilderness: the last line repeats verse 19
decisions.reason: The repeated line closes the prayer and the chapter. The animals join the prophet's cry.

decisions.choice: streams of water: channels in the rock or the valley that normally carry water
decisions.reason: The word is used for watercourses and streambeds. The same word returns in 4:18, where the streambeds of Judah run with water again.

decisions.choice: wild animals (B, R); animals of the field (L)
decisions.reason: "Animals of the field" means wild animals, as Balanced and Readable say. Readable says "cry out" for "pant", the sense the parallel with verse 19 gives.

decisions.choice: bramam (L); anseiam (B)
decisions.reason: The verb is the one of Psalm 42:2 (m1), so each level takes that psalm's Portuguese: "brama" at Literal, the cry of a thirsty animal, and "anseia" at Balanced. Readable says "clamam", as the English "cry out".
